articleTitle: Development of an loT Web-Based Water Temperature Control System for Nano Fish Tanks
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: Nano fish tanks are highly sensitive to temperature fluctuations due to their small water volume, presenting risks to aquatic life. This paper introduces an innovative loT Web-Based Water Temperature Control System that integrates the ESP-32 microcontroller for dynamic temperature regulation with a user-centric web application. The hardware setup, involving temperature sensors and temperature control mechanisms, interacts with a serverless software architecture to maintain ideal aquatic conditions. The system offers real-time data from sensors and interactive controls similar to the Nano tank's physical interface, powered by a cloud-based database and RESTful APIs for robust data management. The LINE Notify API enhances the system by promptly alerting users to temperature anomalies, ensuring the hardware-software integration achieves precise environmental control. Successfully tested in real-world environments, this system provides users with remote access and immediate tank status updates, offering potential for scalability in aquatic care.

articleTitle: Classification of Glaucoma Severity Stages Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: Glaucoma is one of the major causes of blindness worldwide. It can lead to visual loss and poor quality of life. Glaucoma detection, particularly in the early stages, can help prevent blindness if treated promptly. This paper studies the performance of a deep-learning model in the detection of glaucoma severity using fundus photographs. A method based on applying transfer learning to a single pretrained convolutional neural network (CNN) called EfficientNetB7 has been utilized to distinguish between normal, mild/moderate glaucoma, and severe glaucoma, unlike most of the methods where CNN was used to classify only normal and glaucoma classes. The results demonstrated that the model could predict the three classes with the accuracy, specificity, and sensitivity of 88.17%,94.08%, and 88.17%, respectively, which is comparable to the-state-of-the-art deep learning ensemble method but with much less computational cost. The results showed the possi-bility of extending the automatic glaucoma classification from two to three classes without the need to utilize sophisticated techniques.

articleTitle: Designing Appropriate Sensor Values for Surface Forest Fire Alarm Systems Using IoT
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: Forest fire are a common problem today, causing serious damage to people's lives and property safety. It also has a huge impact on the ecological balance and economy of the country. Therefore forest fires are an issue that should be prioritized. Thailand is another country facing this problem, despite being used in the era of modernization of the Internet of Things to help alert forest fires. But one of the reasons for such significant losses is IoT technology. The forest fire alarm is installed in an inappropriate location and delays the alarm, causing serious damage. This paper focuses on using IoT technology to design appropriate sensor values for surface forest fire alarm systems. Since surface fires are the most common type of fires in Thailand, researchers designed an experiment using microcontrollers to work with different sensors for detect surface fire. The system consists of microcontroller, DHT 22 humidity and temperature sensor, MQ-2 gas detection sensor and IR Infrared detector flame sensor. The researchers simulated the surface fire, and then measured the parameters of each sensor under different conditions, and determined the best parameters suitable for the forest fire alarm system based on the Internet of Things, and the result was the optimal temperature value 28.2°c and humidity value is 66.9%. The optimal smoke value is 300 and IR Infrared Detector can detect fire at a distance of up to 1 meter. This result is an initial test. The experimental results will be collected as specified in the next step.

articleTitle: Analyzing Computational Complexity and Footprint: A Comparative Study of State of Charge Estimation across Various Equivalent Circuit Models for Batteries
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: This study delves into the computational complexities and footprints associated with SoC estimation using Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) across a few Equivalent Circuit Models (ECMs): Rint, first-, second-, and third-order models. Through a comparative analysis, we consider the computational demands imposed by each model. The research focuses on understanding the interplay between computational complexity and footprint, shedding light on the trade-offs inherent in choosing an appropriate ECM for SoC estimation. The ECMs under scrutiny are evaluated for their suitability in practical applications. Notably, the results yield a surprising revelation: the footprint in terms of RAM and Flash required by all models remains relatively the same despite the highest optimization level, but the first, second, and third-order models demand 15%, 76%, and 88% more computational time, respectively, compared to the Rint model. Though accuracy is not an issue, the mean error of SoC estimation is consistently below 4 % for all models. In addition, the second and third-order models cause more estimation errors and computational complexity. The results from this research can provide guidance for Battery Management System (BMS) design to trade-off between computational complexity and estimation accuracy.

articleTitle: 0.5-V 16 nW Low-Pass Filter for Bio-Signal Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: This study presents a low-voltage, ultra-low power fully-differential low-pass filter for bio-signal applications using multiple-input fully differential operational transconductance amplifiers (MIFD OTA). This work shows that a low-pass filter using multiple-input OTA can reduce the number of OTAs and power consumption. The low-pass filter can be applied to biomedical signal processing applications. The low-pass filter was simulated using the 0.18 μm (CMOS) technology from TSMC with a supply voltage of 0.5 V. The simulation result shows that the filter has a static power consumption of 16 nW and a 140-Hz bandwidth when operating from a supply voltage of 0.5 V. Input frequency of 10 Hz with an amplitude of 220 mV, the new proposed filter provides a dynamic range of 72.2 dB, total harmonic distortion of 1 %.

articleTitle: Internal AC Heating for Enhancing Lithium Battery Performance in Subzero Temperatures Based on Charge Pump Topology
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: Sub-zero temperatures pose significant challenges for lithium battery, impacting their capacity and performance. Preheating the battery, whether internally or externally, can mitigate these issues. However, internal heating achieves fast, efficient, and uniform heating. This article introduces an internal heating for heating lithium battery through ohmic losses by employing a charge pump to generate AC current. Simulations with an 18650 2.7Ah battery validate the efficacy of this method, demonstrating a remarkable heating rate of 8.26°C per minute with a current RMS of 2.04C at 50KHz while consuming approximately 3.09% of battery capacity.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Multiphase Digital Oscillator
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: This paper presents a design and implementation of the multiphase digital oscillator, which can determine the initial phase of multi-output signals to desired initial phases. The proposed system consists of biquad digital oscillator to oscillate the reference signal, and the new phase shifters which are first order IIR filters that can shift the phase of signals at a specified frequency to give them the desired phases. Design example and simulation results will be shown. Moreover, real-time hardware implementation on STM32 digital signal processor can be demonstrated to confirm the proposed design can work with hardware experimental results.

articleTitle: Open-Source IoT-Integrated SCADA System for Biomass Power Plant Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: This paper presents the development of a condition monitoring system for biomass power plant monitoring, employing the cloud open-source concept combined with notification and security features based on a SCADA system integrated with the IoT. Consequently, the open-source SCADA system is utilized to augment the control system's capabilities. This system will enable interactions among sensors, PLC, SCADA, HMI, and facilitate data storage in a cloud-based database. This integration ensures systematic and organized data collection, fostering efficient data analysis for operational processing within the biomass power plant system. Moreover, it permits rapid problem resolution through notifications via the remote Internet network system.

articleTitle: Recommendation System for Relational Data Using Relational Hard C-Means
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: In several online services, automatic recommendation systems are needed to provide good experiences to users. There are four general recommendation types. One of them is the recommendation system based on the demographics information. Usually, the data used in the recommendation system has a relation among itself. Therefore, we introduced a demographics recommendation system using the relation Hard C-means (RHCM). In particular, the RHCM was applied to segment the data and create multi-prototypes. To make a recommendation, the k-NN was used. We tested our system on a bike sales transactions data set. We found that the average accuracy and Jaccard index for the 1st to 4th test data sets were 0.324 and 0.182, respectively.

articleTitle: Improved Harmonic Detection Delay for Active Power Filter
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: Harmonic elimination using active power filters (APF) is a widely used method in today's electrical systems. Harmonic detection for calculating the reference current for the APF is a critical aspect of harmonic elimination performance. Therefore, this work presents the improved harmonic detection process for the APF with a focus on enhancing harmonic elimination performance. This enhancement takes into consideration the computation delays that arise during the calculation process. Harmonic detection delay can degrade the efficiency of the harmonic elimination system if not considered in the reference current calculation. Therefore, improvements in the delay of harmonic detection are proposed and clearly explained using the sliding window with Fourier analysis (SWFA) technique for harmonic elimination with an APF in single-phase systems as an example. The results confirm that the proposed computation delay improvement provides better harmonic detection performance.

articleTitle: Effects of SIEM Recovery Time: Case Study on Security Onion
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: Security Onion is a widely used open-source SIEM platform built on top of popular open-source security tools like Snort, Suricata, Zeek, and Elasticsearch. It provides features for threat hunting, enterprise security monitoring, and log management. Prolonged recovery time after system failures can increase the vulnerability of the organizations. However, there are many strategies for minimizing recovery time, such as mitigating resource contention during recovery. In this paper, we investigate the factors influencing recovery time, comprising OS startup time and Security Onion service startup time, for both manager and search nodes, focusing on the impact of CPU and I/O contentions. To mimic CPU and I/O contentions, we give VMs a specific CPU budget and I/O bandwidth. Our experiments reveal that the manager node requires longer startup times than the search node due to its more complex startup processes. OS startup time remains relatively consistent across both node types. Both CPU and I/O contentions significantly influence startup time. These findings highlight the importance of resource allocation strategies for Security Onion deployments. Organizations can significantly reduce startup time and ensure rapid recovery of their Security Onion infrastructure.

articleTitle: Fully Automated Charging System for Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: The transition to electric vehicles needs an implementation of suitable charging infrastructure, which can supply increasingly growing vehicle fleets. This requires an improvement of electric grid and energy supply as well as optimization of the charging process itself with the target to enable safe and comfortable access to a wide group of users. In this context, this article focuses on the investigation of a fully automated charging system for electric vehicles.

articleTitle: Advancing In-Pipe Robot Communication with High-Speed OWC Transceiver Front-End Circuit: Experimental Insights and Prospects
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: This paper presents the design and experimentation of a high-speed optical wireless communication front-end transceiver circuit tailored for inpipe robot communication applications. The design process encompasses circuit simulation using the TINA-TI simulation program, PCB fabrication, and subsequent testing within a plastic pipe environment. Experimental findings indicate a system frequency bandwidth of 19.53 MHz for analog modulation at an HB-LED wavelength of 475nm and 300 mA, with an observed attenuation rate of 0.24 dB/cm within the in-pipe setting. Digital modulation experiments yield peak data rates exceeding 50 Mbps for OOK modulation and over 20 Mbps for the PRBS signal. These results hold significant promise for the advancement of optical wireless communication applications in robotics and future 6G communications.

articleTitle: Performance Assessment of Supervised Machine Learning-Based Approaches for Photovoltaic Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: There has been a notable increase in the adoption of solar energy as a sustainable energy choice in recent years due to its positive environmental impact, and widespread availability. However, factors such as weather, component deterioration, improper installation, and maintenance concerns gradually create conditions in the system that threaten its performance and reliability. This study provides a performance evaluation of different supervised machine learning methods for diagnosing photovoltaic cells. Solar power plant datasets containing environmental and electrical parameters were collected, pre-processed, and used to train various machine learning models, including Decision Tree, Long-Short Term Memory, Multilayer Perceptron, Temporal Convolutional Network, Convolutional Neural Network, Naïve Bayes, Support Vector Machine, K-Nearest Neighbor, Random Forest, and Linear Discriminant Analysis algorithms. The models are evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, f1-score, and confusion matrix metrics. Results demonstrated that the models diagnosed short circuit, abnormal voltage, partial shading, and hotspot faults with varying degrees of accuracy.

articleTitle: A Dual Polarization Antenna on Perpendicular Strip Line with Fractal Narrow Slit for GPS, 4G LTE, and 5G Network Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: This article discusses the utilization of a dual polarization antenna on a perpendicular strip line, including a fractal narrow slit, for a global positioning system (GPS), 4G Long Term Evolution (LTE), and a 5G communication network. The proposed antenna consists of a perpendicular strip line that couples the electromagnetic field to a fractal narrow slit, allowing resonance at frequencies of 1.74 GHz and 2.675 GHz. Additionally, it has the capability to facilitate circular polarization for GPS applications and linear polarization for 4G&5G communication networks. The proposed antenna has an impedance characteristic of essentially 22.41% and 9.40% for S11 at frequencies of 1.74 GHz and 2.675 GHz, respectively. At 1.575 GHz, 1.74 GHz, and 2.675 GHz, the antenna's identified peak gains are approximately 2.3 dBi, 2.8 dBi and 3.86 dBi, respectively. Moreover, the proposed antenna has the capability to generate a radiation pattern that propagates in two opposing directions, enabling the efficient exploitation of both GPS and 4G&5G communication network.

articleTitle: Plasmodium Vivax in Thin Blood Smear Classification Using Fuzzy Inference System with Automatic Membership Functions and Rules Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: Malaria can be spread to human by anopheles female mosquitoes. There are four prevalent Plasmodium species responsible for malaria in humans. One of the four species, Plasmodium vivax or P. vivax, is selected in this paper. Its infected cell detection system based on image processing is developed. We automatically generate membership functions of inputs using the possibilistic fuzzy C-means. The Wang-Mendel (WM) method is used to automatically generate rules in the Mamdani fuzzy inference system. Although there are misclassifications because of the wrongly classified cells with similar characteristics to the opposite class, the correct classification rate of the training data is 93.65%. Whereas that of the blind test data set is 99.58%.

articleTitle: Assessment of Self-Mixing Interferometric Technique for Displacement Sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: Self-mixing interferometric (SMI) technique has demonstrated its effectiveness in achieving precise and contactless measurements of submicron displacements. Comprehensive assessments of its effectiveness in displacement sensing, particularly in scenarios involving dynamic targets with varying displacements and frequencies remain as a gap. In this work, we introduce an optoelectronic testbed that includes the fundamental setup of the self-mixing interferometer, incorporating a controllable piezoelectric actuator as the target to assess the effectiveness of the SMI technique in sensing the displacement. We provide detailed insights into the construction of the transimpedance-amplifier and calibration parameters of the optoelectronic setup. Utilizing the proposed testbed, our experiments demonstrate the capability to sense displacements within the range of 0.325 μm to 2.925 μm. Our study significantly advances the understanding of the SMI technique's applicability in displacement sensing, particularly in dynamic scenarios, highlighting its potential as an adaptable and effective technique for submicron displacement measurements across diverse applications and fields.

articleTitle: Comparison of Different Deep Learning Networks to Classify Epilepsy Seizure Based on EEG Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: Epilepsy, a widespread neurological condition impacting approximately 50 million people worldwide, is often identified and studied through electroencephalography (EEG) due to its rich temporal information. Convolutional neural networks and recurrent neural networks have demonstrated potential in automatically detecting seizures from EEG data. Despite this, there's a shortage of comprehensive studies comparing the detection capabilities of different designs. This research assesses and contrasts the effectiveness of five renowned deep neural network models - CNN, LSTM, BiLSTM, GRU, and BiGRU - in binary categorization of EEG segments into seizure and non-seizure groups. Training and evaluation utilize the publicly accessible Bonn dataset, specifically crafted for epileptic seizure detection. Performance metrics like accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score are employed in the analysis. The principal findings highlight BiGRU's impressive accuracy at 95.80% and F1-score at 92.96% in individualized seizure identification. Additionally, the study introduces a groundbreaking deep learning architecture, the self-normalizing neural network (SNN), to enhance seizure detection accuracy. The recommended SNN exhibits outstanding performance, boasting an accuracy of 98.50% and an impressive F1-score of 98.50%.

articleTitle: A VR System of Slide Position Self-Learning with Controllers Position Detection and Tactile Feedback for Trombone Beginners
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: This paper proposes a VR-based self-practicing system of a trombone for beginners. Adopting hand controllers with 6DOF as input and VR HMD with speaker and tactile device on the hand controllers as output, the proposed system provides visual, acoustic and tactile sense for feedback of correct/incorrect position of the slide of trombone. Through the experience of the proposed system, the learners are expected to recognize the correct positions of a slide corresponding sound scales. A user test with pre/post questionnaire shows good performance of the proposed system.

articleTitle: Development of Lighting from LED Lamps for Growing Chrysanthemum Flowers
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: This study investigates the use of LED lighting for the cultivation of Chrysanthemum flowers, aiming to identify the most suitable LED bulb for optimal growth and blooming. Three greenhouses were utilized for the experiment: the first relying on sunlight, the second employing LED light-emitting diode bulbs, and the third utilizing LED solar cell spotlights, both powered by solar cell sets. Chrysanthemum growth was monitored, maintaining a minimum light intensity of 80 lux across all greenhouses. Results indicated that Chrysanthemum flowers exhibited the most significant growth in the greenhouse illuminated by LED solar cell spotlights, with an average height of 27 cm and an average flower diameter of 1.5 cm. The second-best growth occurred in the greenhouse using LED light-emitting diode bulbs, resulting in an average height of 25 cm and an average flower diameter of 0.9 cm. Conversely, the greenhouse relying solely on sunlight demonstrated the least growth, with an average height of 15 cm and an average flower diameter of 0.6 cm. Notably, the orange light emitted by the spotlights proved to be the most effective photoperiod for optimal Chrysanthemum growth, as it corresponds to the wavelength most efficiently absorbed by plants.

articleTitle: Modified ChannelNet for Estimating SISO-OFDM Channels
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: We propose to modify ChannelNet, which is a convolutional neural network (CNN) used to estimate fast-fading channels in orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM). By replacing linear interpolation with zero padding and removing the denoising CNN, we significantly reduce the computational complexity of the estimation with minimal performance degradation. The numerical results confirm that the proposed modifications can achieve a comparable mean square error (MSE) performance close to the linear minimum MSE estimation.

articleTitle: 0.5-V Mixed-Mode Universal Active Filter Using Multiple-Input OTAs
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: This study introduces new 0.5 V, ultra-low power mixed-mode universal analog filter applying multiple-input operational transconductance amplifiers (MI-OTAs). The filter configuration based on MI-OTAs and two grounded capacitors to actualize a mixed-mode universal filter that can produce four modes second-order filters, that is low-pass, high-pass, band-pass, band-stop and all-pass filters, namely voltage-mode, current-mode, transimpedance mode, transconductance-mode, by appropriate selecting input signals. The filter's natural frequency can be electronically controlled. The mixed-mode filter was analyzed using CMOS 0.18μm process simulation from TSMC, operating with a 0.5 V power supply.

articleTitle: A Traffic Monitoring Method Using Accumulative Difference Images
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: This paper presents a traffic monitoring method to count the number of vehicles from video surveillance on a highway. The proposed method uses the accumulative difference images (ADI) for extracting the vehicles from stationary background scenes. The result of ADI is a sequence of images, namely, x-y planes. However, we cannot count the number of vehicles in full frame directly because the vehicles far from the video camera are small and occluded. The horizontal-temporal cross-section plane is applied for ADI result that is the 3-D data (x, y, t) to slice into y-t plane at a certain level of x to observe the moving object or vehicles on video within one frame. To count the number of vehicles in cross-section planes within 1-D projection, we propose to separate the lanes of the road to avoid missing vehicles caused by connection of vehicles that extracted from original video. The result shows that counting the number of vehicles with full frame on x-y planes is less accurate by the video environment than we propose to use horizontal-temporal cross-section method to observe the y-t planes.

articleTitle: The Virtual Service Center For Telecommunication Business Enhancement Using Metaverse
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: This paper presents the first 3D Virtual Service Center of National Telecom Public Company Limited (NT), Thailand. The major aims of constructing the digital twin of the service center at the headquarters are to provide customers with new engaging and immersive experiences and to decrease excessive work for employees in the service center. The virtual service center includes features such as an interactive learning simulation of service procedures, demonstrations of the products with animated guidance, and live chat support for realtime communication with NT staff. The preliminary qualitative survey was conducted with undergraduate students at Chulalongkorn University. The feedback has been positive, which includes the immersive quality of the virtual environment, the ease of navigation, the quality of social interaction, and the well-executed. This comprehensive strategy offers a novel and captivating way for customers to engage with the business while also improving customer understanding and service center efficiency.

articleTitle: A Surveillance System Utilizing mmWave-FMCW Radar for Restricted Control Area
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: In this paper, we introduce a surveillance system utilizing mmWave-FMCW radar designed for restricted control areas. The experiment, conducted in our laboratory, defines the restricted control area parameters. Employing the TI-IWR6843AOPEVM model, operating at 60–64 GHz, and providing point cloud and Doppler information, we assumed walking paths for testing, partitioning scenarios into four distinct cases to simulate real-world scenarios. System performance evaluation, assessed through confusion matrices, demonstrates an achieved accuracy of up to 76.9%. Notably, errors are mainly caused by multipath effects due to static objects within the testing environment.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Support Vector Regression with Grey Wolf Optimization in Stock Market Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: The stock market price is influenced by many factors both domestic and international factors. To help stock traders in make buying or selling decision, a stock price prediction model is needed. In this paper, a stock closing price prediction system is introduced. We utilized 17 financial factors, i.e., 8 technical analysis factors (Crude oil price, Gold spot, Thai Baht to US Dollar exchange rate, High price, Low price, Opening price, Closing price, and Volume) and 9 fundamental factors (Exponential moving average, Relative strength index, Current ratio, Return on equity ratio, Return on assets ratio, Net profit margin ratio, Debt to equity ratio, Price to earning ratio, and Price to book value) from 18 previous working days as our inputs. We then computed chaos centroids from each factor. Finally, to predict the Monday closing price, the fuzzy support vector regression with the grey wolf optimization is utilized. There are 29 companies in 6 industry groups, i.e., RESOURCE, SERVICE, INDUS, PROPCON, AGRO, and TECH, considered in this research. We found that the minimum root mean square error of the blind test set is 0.3698 and the maximum of that is 11.66. However, the prediction trend of each company is very similar to the real closing price.

articleTitle: Emulation of Novel and Electronically Tunable Universal Mem-Elements Design
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: This study proposes the use of an active building block Operational Transconductance Amplifier (OTA), 6 MOS transistors, and a few passive components to design an electronically tunable universal mem-elements emulator circuit that includes memristor (MR), memcapacitor (MC), and meminductor (MI). Mem element's physical realization is still an open challenge that drives the creation of new designs. The universal circuit requires one floating resistor and two grounded capacitors as passive components. The topology of mem-elements has been implemented using a switch without altering the circuit structure. The workability of memristor and meminductor don't require any resistor while memcapacitor requires the use of one resistor. The presented design establishes a simple mathematical relationship and verifies Memristive system fingerprint traits such as pinched hysteresis loop (PHL). The theoretical propositions of MR, MC, and MI have been accompanied by a variety of modeling. The MR, MC, and MI emulation circuits use 7.4 mW, 11.2 mW, and 10.4 mW of power, respectively.

articleTitle: The Effects of the Grain Sizes and the Heat Spot Geometry on the Transition Jitter in HAMR Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: Thermal profile is one of the main factors that determine the shape of the magnetic footprint in heat-assisted magnetic recording (HAMR) technology. The characteristics of the magnetic footprint are one of the factors that influence the formation of the zig-zag or transition boundary in the two-dimensional (2-D) format. The transition boundary is calculated to obtain the transition jitter. The performance of HAMR technology can be identified by the transition jitter. In this work, transition boundary in 2-D format is used to identify the effect of the thermal profile. The thermal profile models are squircle, circle, and ellipse. Micromagnetic simulation based on the Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation is used in the recording process. Moreover, grain size is investigated to determine the transition jitter. It was found that the squircle with grain size of 3 nm has the lowest average transition jitter.

articleTitle: A Binary Hexagon Stripe Metamaterial Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: This paper presents the numerical simulation of the hexagonal-based binary-coding metamaterial antennas in the centimeter-wave band (7–24 GHz) for 6G communication. Two types of unit cells are created by an opposite reflection phase as digital binary “0” and “1” elements. The engineered planar configuration is referred to as a hexagon-based artificial magnetic conductor (AMC) with a vertical stripe pattern. The field source is excited by using an aperture-fed structure with a microstrip line. The advancement of this configuration is that wideband and double band with distinct radiation patterns. The proposed antenna object comes up with a widened impedance bandwidth due to using a hexagonal patch and optimizing the impedance matching of the mutual coupling effect. The full-wave simulation based on the FEM method is used to study the characteristics of antenna performance. The resultant antennas can be operated at the targeted frequency of 7~9 GHz. The simulated results report the characteristics of scattering and field distribution in terms of reflection, impedance, current configuration, and radiation patterns.

articleTitle: Joint Position and Orientation Estimation for Visible Light Positioning Using Extended Kalman Filters
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: In this work, an extended Kalman filter (EKF) is applied to solve the problem of joint estimation of object position and orientation for indoor visible light positioning (VLP) systems. It is assumed that light emitting diode (LED) lamps are installed on the room ceiling, with their illuminations following the Lambertian emission pattern. A receiver is located on the floor, with three photo diodes (PDs) mounted on a pyramid structure. Mathematical expressions for EKF related computations are derived. Numerical results from 10,000 random receiver positions and orientations in an 8m-by-8m area under nine LED lamps are used to evaluate the estimation accuracy. The results indicate that, in the considered room scenario, the position estimation error is within 0.18 m while the orientation estimation error is within 12.5 degree for 95% of the time. Finally, object tracking using the EKF is demonstrated when the receiver moves along a circular path, indicating a potential of EKF based joint position and orientation estimation in a dynamic environment.

articleTitle: From Stress to Growth: Plant Hormonal and Physiological Responses to Microwave Radiation
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: This research is being conducted to examine the impact of radiofrequency (RF) waves on plant growth, considering both advantages and disadvantages. Specific studies suggest that manipulating radio frequency (RF) and intensities can enhance plant growth and increase productivity. This effect could be attributed to enhanced water and nutrient uptake, as well as the activation of stress responses and developmental gene expression. Additional studies have shown that higher levels of RF or prolonged periods of exposure may lead to a decrease in growth, abnormalities in physical structure, and damage to cells. RF has situation-dependent effects on plant development. In order to apply RF technology in agriculture in a responsible manner, it is necessary to conduct additional research to gain a better understanding of the underlying processes, determine the optimal parameters for beneficial applications, and establish limitations for undesirable effects. This study quantifies the development of plants, as well as their electrical conductivity (EC) and pH levels, in response to stress caused by the injection of more energy and their isolation from exposure to electromagnetic waves. The results are fascinating.

articleTitle: The Compatible Partial Response Maximum Likelihood Detection Schemes for Blu-ray Discs
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: The global datasphere is experiencing significant expansion, largely driven by the relentless advancement of artificial intelligence technology. Cold data, in particular, is garnering increasing attention and is now considered a vital asset, constituting a substantial portion of data capacity. Optical discs stand out as a highly promising solution for cold data archiving due to their robust data security, longevity, durability, and non-volatile nature. Additionally, their total cost of operation (TCO) further enhances their appeal. To increase the recording density, signal processing techniques must evolve along with the degradation of signal quality. In this paper, we conduct a comprehensive study of partial response maximum likelihood (PRML) detection based on simulation and real signal testing and compare an adaptive equalized detection scheme with a neural network equalized detection method for BD-ROM and BDXL systems. Results show the effectiveness of PRML method for both BD-ROM and BDXL. The neural network equalized detection method can also improve the detection performance of BD-ROM and BDXL at lower signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) levels.

articleTitle: Analysis of a ZVDS Class-DE Current-Driven Full-Bridge Rectifier to Compensation Network Capacitance Design for WPT System
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: The accurate, systematic, and effective design method of compensation network capacitance based on the series-series resonant topology is presented for reducing reactive power of wireless power transfer system. The design procedure uses a principle of the current-driven Class-DE full-bridge zero-voltage and zero-derivative-switching rectifier, a Class-D full-bridge zero-voltage-switching inverter, and a loosely coupling transformer. The key parameters of the Class-DE current-driven full-bridge zero-voltage and zero-derivative-switching rectifier as a function of diode duty ratio are derived from the time-domain analysis with Fourier series, such as the normalized input impedance and relationship of input current and output voltage. Moreover, the presented topology has a soft-switching conditions that low-switching losses as well as low-switching noise. The presented design is verified by experiments, the maximum transfer power and system efficiency at a transfer distance of 50 mm are 1.8 kW and 93.38%, respectively.

articleTitle: Robust Practical Fixed-Time Control and Application to DC-DC Buck Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: This work presents an adaptive fixed-time speed controller of permanent magnet synchronous motors for a class of second-order nonlinear systems based on practical fixed-time stability, in which a sliding mode surface with a constant exponent coefficient is designed to avoid singularities and achieve a fast convergence rate. This method is easy to implement compared to other sophisticated fixed-time controllers. In addition, the upper bound of control inputs is selected to prevent saturation limitations. Following that, the Lyapunov function expresses the close-loop stability of a practical fixed-time controller. An adaptive disturbance rejection with smooth function is presented to attenuate the total disturbances, chattering, and steady-state error. The tracking error is integrated into a bounded residual region within a specified time. Finally, numerical simulations are given to verify the performance of both controller and disturbance rejection mechanisms.

articleTitle: EV Charging Demand Estimation in Residential Areas: Workday Commute Case Studies
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: The rapid increasing of electric vehicles in suburbs residential areas poses a significant challenge for low-voltage grids due to uncoordinated charging demands, potentially exceeding transformer capacity. This paper presents a data-driven framework for EV power demand forecasting, leveraging dynamic travel patterns and personalized driving data to overcome limitations of existing statistical models. Implemented as a MATLAB-based simulation software, the software integrates diverse data sources like Google Maps API and OpenWeather API to predict charging events with granularity. Numerical studies based on workday commute scenarios between suburbs and capital areas reveal that uncoordinated charging can lead to peak demands exceeding transformer capacity.

articleTitle: FuseFiction: Bridging Ideas to Plots with Mobile Apps for Novice Writers
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: This study introduces FuseFiction, a user-friendly, cross-platform mobile application developed with Flutter for Android and iOS compatibility. Designed specifically for novice fiction writers, it incorporates seven foundational narrative structures to aid in educational plot development. The app also provides character management tools and features to help writers outline and adhere to schedules. Robust data handling is ensured through Firebase. Currently undergoing user testing, the application emphasizes intuitive UX and UI. Initial feedback highlights its ease of use (average rating of 4.51, standard deviation of 0.56) and practical value (average rating of 3.99, standard deviation of 0.74). Aimed at providing fiction writers with an accessible platform, FuseFiction supports plot creation, character development, and writing schedule organization. Through continuous user feedback and iterative design, it aspires to become an essential educational tool, enhancing narrative skills and fostering creativity in novice writers.

articleTitle: Eye Landmarks Detection using RT-DETR with Rules
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: In order to help ophthalmologists diagnose eye problems, it is necessary to scan for eye landmarks such as the pupil, the reflection point on the retina, and the boundary of the eye. An individual's eye landmarks on their face can be obtained via some facial landmarks' detection methods, including Haar Cascade. Two problematic aspects of the current approaches, however, are that the pupil and reflection point information is not provided, and the detection is ineffective when confronted with a picture of the upper half of the face or a person wearing a mask. In this study, we intend to develop a deep learning model for eye landmark identification using the Realtime identification Transformer (RT-DETR) approach together with our rules. As a consequence, nine landmark points-two for the eye, six for the pupil, and one for the reflection, are computed with an accuracy of 0.974. Since the focus of this paper is on eye landmark recognition, the next stage will be to build an application and a machine learning model for the diagnosis of eye disorders. - Keywords Deep Learning, Detection, Eye Landmarks, Facial Landmarks, Ophthalmology, RT-DETR

articleTitle: A Schmitt Trigger Independently/Electronically Controllable Upper and Lower Threshold Currents
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: This article presents a current-mode Schmitt trigger circuit using commercial ICs and NOT gates. This circuit can be electronically controlled and operated independently to adjust the output amplitude and the threshold current in the upper and lower levels. Performance testing of the proposed circuit through PSpice simulations reveals that the output amplitude upper and lower threshold currents can be controlled effectively using external bias currents, corresponding to the theoretical analysis. Additionally, the presented circuit illustrates stability to external variations in temperature.

articleTitle: Enhancing Clinical Activity Recognition with Bidirectional RNNs and Accelerometer-ECG Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: The ongoing monitoring of human activities has several applications in digital health. However, precisely identifying activities in medical settings is difficult because of the intricate nature of actions and patient differences. This study presents a sophisticated approach using deep learning to combine accelerometer and ECG data from wearable devices to identify clinical activities. The suggested approach involves using a dual-stream convolutional-recurrent neural network to capture spatial and temporal patterns accurately. An assessment was carried out using a dataset that is accessible to the public, including records of activities undertaken by both healthy individuals and patients diagnosed with pneumoconiosis. An analysis was conducted on five deep learning architectures, which included convolutional, recurrent, and bidirectional recurrent networks. The results demonstrated that bidirectional gated recurrent units exhibited the most fantastic accuracy, ranging from 97% to 99%, for both the healthy and sick categories. This performance is significantly above that of the long short-term memory and convolutional neural network models. The results indicate that combining convolutional feature extraction and bidirectional sequential modeling allows for the effective learning of valuable features from multi-modal clinical time-series data. The results enhance the monitoring of human activities in clinical settings by combining specific deep neural networks designed for mobile health applications.

articleTitle: Optimization of Transmit Beamforming Using Channel Covariances for MISO Downlink Assisted by Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: We propose an unsupervised beamforming neural network (BNN) to optimize transmit beamforming in downlink multiple input single output (MISO) channels. Reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) panels are used to assist user equipment that does not receive sufficiently s trong s ignals f rom t he base station. To avoid frequent beam updates, the proposed BNN is based on slow-changing channel covariances and is different from most other BNNs that utilize instant channel state information. Numerical simulations show that the proposed BNN can achieve much higher sum rates than zeroforcing beamforming does when the system is heavily loaded and can drastically reduce computation time for large-scale communication systems.

articleTitle: MO-CCCII High-Order Chebyshev Notch Filter
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: This article presents the design of a high-order Chebyshev notch filter using Multiple Output Current Controlled Conveyor (MO-CCCII). In this design process, the RLC high-order low-pass Chebyshev filter prototype is initially converted into a notch filter by using network transform. Subsequently, passive network analyses were performed using Kirchhoff's Current Law (KCL) method and Signal Flow Graph (SFG). Lossy and lossless integrators/differentiators using MO-CCCIIs are designed to substitute in the SFG. The performances of the proposed circuit are simulated by using PSpice. The proposed filter can effectively reject the frequency 50Hz-80Hz. The results also provide the electronically tunable feature by removing the powerline interference of 50Hz and 60Hz systems in biosensor applications.

articleTitle: Location Aware and Drift Control Using a Smartphone On-board an Unmanned Aerial Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: Smartphones and Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs), regarded as consumer-grade technologies, offer a remarkable price/performance ratio, making their integration a strategic approach for maximizing overall performance. Our work addresses the complex challenges of UAV navigation in GPS-denied and enclosed environments for estimating the exact relative position by proposing an integration of a smartphone-based aerial platform. The selected control strategy and estimation, demonstrates enhanced robustness in diverse indoor and outdoor environments, showcasing precision and managing uncertainty by reducing the sensory drift taking into account the motion dynamics of the UAV. This study underscores the challenges of UAV navigation in GPS-denied settings, emphasizing the significance of sensor fusion and advanced estimation techniques. Our devised strategies aim to keep a balanced tradeoff between the estimation and motion model of the aerial platform. This research could lay the groundwork for advancing UAV technology, providing solutions to real-world challenges in GPS-denied and enclosed spaces.

articleTitle: Tri-Beam UHF-RFID Tag Antenna for Indoor Asset Tracking
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: This paper proposes a multi-beam UHF RFID tag antenna for indoor localization and tracking. Three dipole structures are placed on a dielectric substrate with hexagonal shape. To distinguish the angle of detection, an equilateral triangle reflector is centrally situated with all sides in parallel with the printed dipoles on the same substrate. This allows distinction between the beams corresponding to each dipole. The antenna is simulated using CST MW studio. NXP UCODE G2iL passive RFID chips are used to conjugately match with the input impedance of the dipole antennas. The radiation patterns show separation between the main lobe of the beams apart by θ = 120° with a radiation efficiency of 29%. A back-reflector representing the top area of a moving robot is also added to elevate the beams to enhance tag antenna's detection footprint. With the back reflector, the main-lobe orientation is elevated to θ= 35° with a 25.21 % radiation efficiency.

articleTitle: Strategy to Prevent Overload of Transformer in Distribution System with High Penetration of Electric Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: Though technological advancements bring convenience to humans, they also pose environmental damage. EVs are an alternative that tackles these concerns. However, the growing popularity of EVs is starting to cause problems in distribution systems, especially when the uncoordinated charging of EVs in each house risks overloading distribution transformers. This paper proposes efficient strategies for managing EV chargers in houses. In the event of transformer overload, the proposed control system will control the EV chargers of each house to decrease the power output. However, consumers have an option to pay an additional fee to retain the privilege of charging their EVs without any reduction in power output. Consumers who do not pay an additional fee will experience a proportional reduction in power output. This strategy provides an option for consumers who require charging urgently. To test the effectiveness of the proposed method, this paper utilized two test systems. The first test system is a seven-bus system featuring a 100-kVA distribution transformer, and the second test system is an IEEE European LV feeder featuring a 500-kVA distribution transformer. Test results indicate that the proposed strategy can prevent overload of distribution transformers. This approach helps alleviate concerns about the increasing demand for EV charging in numerous houses during peak usage times.

articleTitle: Using VR to Enhance Real-World Engagement to Supplement Service Design Process
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: Post-2020, the service economy has evolved from mere service experiences to experience transformation. Converting occasional guests into loyal customers has become a daily challenge for businesses in terms of service innovation. This paper delves into the utilization of panoramic imaging technology and multi-perspective viewpoints to achieve the perspective of “rendering authenticity” in the experience economy. Furthermore, it proposes the application of these technologies in the service design process to deliver authentic experiences to stakeholders. Addressing the challenges of non-physical touchpoints, this paper presents a service design workflow integrating digital curating tools and showcases its outcomes. The process involves the use of a 360-degree panoramic camera, a panoramic VR application development platform, VR headsets, and a design thinking-guided self-directed experimental course module. Field verification was conducted in General Village and Chang'an Street in Hsinchu City. The entire process includes touchpoint experience collection, co-creation of experience touchpoints, service prototype curating, and sustainable presentation of service concepts. This process aligns with the trend of digital curating, which includes providing a platform to render authenticity and connect businesses, design teams, and service co-creation stakeholders, ultimately delivering “the moment of truth”. Following practical validation of service design in cultural regeneration areas, this study found that the introduction of digital curating tools into service design enables design teams and stakeholders to co-create more refined experiences. Its advantages are threefold: firstly, it augments authenticity, assisting design teams and co-creation stakeholders in designing experiences authentically; secondly, it provides design teams with new perspectives, extending new touchpoints from existing ones; thirdly, it preserves workshop outcomes in panoramic VR curation formats, ensuring the sustainability of co-creation. Overall, digital curating tools offer convenience in accessing authentic rendering environments, guide possibilities for stakeholder co-creation, and extend the sustainability of service design. Digital integration extends beyond digitizing texts; it brings new opportunities for service design.

articleTitle: Electronically Tunable Three-Input Single-Output Fully Differential Universal Filter Employing Commercially Available ICs
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: The four Multiple-Input Operational Transconductance Amplifier (MI-OTA) used in this paper's electronically tunable three-input, single-output fully differential universal filter is built using two commercially available integrated circuits (ICs) (LM13700), two capacitors, and two resistors. The proposed circuit provides all five standard filter functions; it is possible to select one without modifying the circuit topology by adjusting the input signal condition. The features of the circuit are the ability of the natural frequency and quality factor, which can be tuned via the capacitor. Included are the simulation results, which validate the suggested circuit's operation. The data presented closely aligns with the theoretical prediction.

articleTitle: A Graph-based Data Mining Approach for Template Recognition using Large Log Datasets in Software Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: Log files generated by software systems can be utilized as a valuable resource in data-driven approaches to improve the system health and stability. These files often contain valuable information about runtime execution, and their effective monitoring requires analyzing an increasingly large volume of data logs. In this paper, a graph mining technique for log parsing is presented, which is source agnostic to the system. This means that the technique can function regardless of the source of the logs, making it more scalable and reusable. Unlike the existing approaches that rely heavily on domain knowledge and regular expression patterns, the proposed approach uses graph models and semantic analysis to detect data patterns with minimal user input. This makes it easy to implement it in a variety of scenarios where application-based logs may differ significantly. The proposed parsing technique is evaluated over seven datasets. It achieves the best performance on the Thunderbird dataset, where the technique takes 3.87 seconds for 2000 logs, while obtaining precision, recall and F1 measure higher than 0.99.

articleTitle: The Dynamical Modeling of Four Mecanum Wheel Mobile Robot on Typical Unstructured Terrain
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: Omni-directional mobile platforms, particularly those equipped with Mecanum wheels, have revolutionized robotics research by enabling advanced mobility in various settings. This paper focuses on the kinematic and dynamic modeling of a four mecanum wheel mobile robot (FMWMR) on inclined surfaces, a terrain type that presents unique challenges. The kinematic model captures the intricate relationship between wheel velocities and the robot's overall motion, crucial for precise control. Additionally, the dynamic model, derived using Lagrange's equations, accounts for the influence of gravity and other forces on the robot's movement. Numerical simulations under different slope conditions reveal how the robot's trajectory and orientation are affected, providing insights into its behavior on sloped terrains

articleTitle: Enhancing On-Device Multiple Face Recognition for Class Attendance based on Flutter Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: Face recognition is a notable technology which can be utilized to check on the presence of students in the class. Almost all existing face recognition mobile applications can only recognize one student per frame, which would only be efficient for a small number of students. To address this issue, we propose an offline mobile application that can recognize multiple faces for attendance checking, which is performed by a pretrained ResNet50-based VGGFace2 dataset. In this study, different fine-tuning ResNet50 approaches were proposed to determine the most suitable model for on-device inference. The performance of these approaches was tested for recognizing varying numbers of faces. Their performance was tested for recognizing varying numbers of faces. The results were measured in terms of precision, recall, F-measure, accuracy, and processing time in seconds. The results suggest that the best number of faces that can be accurately recognized could be 15 students in one frame using the different fine-tuning ResNet50 approaches, which achieve over 80% accuracy.

articleTitle: Low-Cost Technique for Extracting the Cole-Cole Model Parameters
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: This paper proposed a new efficient approach for extracting the parameters of the Cole-Cole impedance model. The main offered advantage is simple and low-cost but accurate in identifying the constant phase element from the bioimpedance models. The Cole-Cole model is simplified as a low-pass filter (LPF) by using a few electronic components. The magnitude and phase response of LPF characteristics are applied to calculate the fractional order (α) and value of the capacitor. This technique offers low complexity and low-cost equipment. The circuit can be realized by a low-component count based on a single OPAMP and four resistors. PSpice simulation with a Cole model is carried out to verify the method. The simulation results are in good agreement with the theory expectations.

articleTitle: Identification of Unstable Linear Systems using Data-driven Koopman Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: System identification plays a crucial role in modern control techniques, enabling the data-driven learning of input-output maps or mathematical models. However, practical applications face challenges as the actual number of states is often unknown, and observed variables may be limited. Additionally, unstable systems present further difficulties, as their outputs rapidly diverge or saturate, hindering long-term measurement. This paper addresses these challenges by proposing a novel input-aware modeling method for unstable linear systems using data-driven Koopman analysis. Unlike traditional Koopman analysis which focuses solely on state dynamics, our method explicitly incorporates the influence of the input function <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$u(t)$</tex>. This enables us to accurately capture the complete behavior of the system, even under the influence of external control signals. By leveraging Koopman operator theory on augmented state-input data, we capture both the intrinsic dynamics and the sensitivity to external control, crucial for accurate prediction and control of unstable systems. This input-aware approach extends the capabilities of data-driven Koopman analysis to improve modeling and control of complex unstable systems in various applications.

articleTitle: Design of Circularly Polarized Rounded Corner Square Patch Antenna with Shallow Slot for UHF RFID Reader Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: Design of circularly polarized rounded corner square patch antenna with shallow slot for UHF RFID reader applications is proposed. The circularly polarized antenna is designed to support the radio frequency identification (RFID) systems in the UHF band and has a unidirectional pattern. The designed antenna has circular polarization covering the frequency band 920-925MHz, which makes it suitable for UHF RFID systems. And importantly, the proposed antenna has been designed with an off-center-feed point in the xy-plane at the feed x = 30, y = 30 position. And the rounded corner square patch technique with a radius equal to 21mm and the shallow slot grooving technique were applied together to make the proposed antenna have the desired electrical characteristics. In this case, the proposed antenna consists of a 132x132mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> square patch stacked with a 200x200mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> ground plane, with an air barrier between the square patch and the ground plane. The simulated ∣S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>∣(dB) of the proposed antenna covering the 906-936MHz frequency band. The Axial-Ratio (AR) bandwidth is less than 3dB covering the 920-925MHz frequency band.

articleTitle: The Prototypes of Classified Products via Digital Image Correlation
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: This paper describes the creation process, design, and construction of an automatic object color sorting machine, which utilizes a web camera to detect the color of objects on a conveyor belt. An Arduino board and a LabViewprogram control the machine. The machine aims to sort out objects of different colors, specifically red, blue, green, and yellow. The automatic movement of objects is achieved using an Arduino board. In contrast, the webcam color object detector reads the light intensity that hits the object and is reflected to the webcam. The level of difference according to each object's color can be specified. The research can be utilized as a guideline for industrial plants that work on color separation of objects employed in production to classify objects of different colors as the program commands. This automatic movement system effectively sorts red, blue, green, and yellow objects. The system is programmed to recognize red and blue as bad and green and yellow as good. The data can be stored as an Excel file and show the average value of the color objects tested. The error value of the system is deficient, making it a highly reliable and accurate system. In determination, the research results of the automatic color sorting machine using a web camera on the conveyor belt are effectively related. The system's performance in sorting objects based on color is highly efficient and accurate. This system can be utilized in various industries, such as food production plants, automobile factories, and electronic components factories. The results experiment, The F-measure, which balanced the prediction accuracy in the target group (Precision) and the Recall, was used to evaluate the model's overall performance. The system's accuracy is 98.68 percent, and the system can classify products.

articleTitle: Low-Noise and High Linearity Potentiostat for Implantable Rumen pH Sensor Using Current Mirror Combined with Chopper Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: This work presents a low-noise and high linearity potentiostat design used for biomedical implantable rumen pH sensor applications by using current mirror combined with chopper technique. The potentiostat is designed to regulates the potential thought the negative feedback loop. In the design, a folded cascode control amplifier was realized a PMOS-input single stage single-ended op-amp. The control amplifier provided a DC gain over 42.89 dB. The chopper technique was also employed to reduce low-frequency noise and increase system stability. The proposed potentiostat was designed on a standard 0.13 um CMOS process. The was simulated results showed that the potentiometer power consumption less was than 78 μW and generated a sensor current in the range of 44.58-361.82 nA with the varied impedance Z<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">WE</inf>. These results indicate that this topology is a promising candidate for a low-power implantable biomedical application.

articleTitle: Development of an Exercise Posture Monitoring System for Air Cadets by Using MediaPipe and OpenCV
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of standardizing the pulling posture test at the Air Force School, a crucial element in evaluating physical fitness and a key factor in selecting aviation cadets. The existing problem stems from the lack of standardization, as the scoring of the pulling posture test relies on the subjective judgment of the evaluation committee. To tackle this issue, this paper proposes a systematic approach to standardize and establish consistent criteria for the pulling posture test. We introduce a novel system for assessing students' pulling postures, leveraging MediaPipe and OpenCV technologies. Our system involves programming and utilizing MediaPipe and OpenCV modules to access the camera and detect facial features, hand movements, and angles of both arms. When a participant performs the pulling motion, the system evaluates whether it meets predefined criteria. Successful attempts trigger an auditory confirmation, and the system automatically records and logs the count. To validate the accuracy of our system, we conducted tests in which instructors manually counted alongside the automated system. The results indicate the system's capabilities to accurately detect pulling postures, although further development is necessary to address challenges related to camera height and angle. Our findings suggest that this system holds promise in standardizing the pulling posture test, providing a valuable tool for the selection of aviation cadets at the Air Force School.

articleTitle: VCII-Based Transimpedance-Mode All Pass Filter using Single Grounded Capacitor
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: This paper describes a first-order transimpedance-mode all-pass filter (APF) based on single grounded capacitor and second-generation voltage conveyors (VCIIs). The proposed APF comprises 3 VCIIs cooperating with 5 resistors and 1 grounded capacitor, it is consequently suitable to integrated circuit implementation. The phase angle of the output relative to input signals can be tuned by the external resistors. In addition, the amplitude of output voltage can be linearly controllable by a resistor. The output current can also be achieved to offer current-mode APF without changing circuit topology. The proposed APF offers a phase shifting function over a wide range of operating frequency. Its output also provides an accurate sinusoidal signal. The testing results obtained from PSpice simulation are disclosed to investigate different behaviors of the proposed APF. From the results, it is found that they are agreed well with the mentioned anticipations, where its total power consumption is about 1.02mW at ±1.2V supply voltages.

articleTitle: ECG Signal Analysis Techniques using Digital Filter with Deep Learning in Unbiased Data
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: Electrocardiogram (ECG) can be used in various ways, especially in the classification of cardiovascular diseases with deep learning technology. Nowadays deep learning technology has been developed by many ideas through time to create an effective model. This paper presented pre-processing method by removing biased in data and filtering data before using them in deep learning to increase the classification accuracy. This deep learning process can categorize cardiovascular diseases in 5 conditions by using Lead II ECG signal in PhysioNet's MIT-BIH and PTB Diagnostic ECG datasets with Median, Butterworth, Chebyshev I, Chebyshev II, and Elliptic for digital filtering. The evaluation after deep learning delivered the accuracy as follows: 97.4% in Median, 98.6% in Butterworth, 97.8% in Chebyshev I, 97.2% in Chebyshev II, and 97.2% in Elliptic. Moreover, the factor of deep learning accuracy depends on biased and configuration of digital filters that will be detailed in the result and discussion.

articleTitle: Enhanced Monte Carlo Simulation for PV Hosting Capacity Evaluation in Low Voltage Distribution
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: The growing trend of residential solar photovoltaic (PV) systems highlights the need for accurate photovoltaic hosting capacity (PVHC) evaluation method in low-voltage distribution networks. This study aims to improve the precision of PVHC which is calculated by Monte Carlo-based method using a proposed hybrid linear and binary search approach. In addition, the weighted load concept is introduced for more accurate PVHC. The simulation of a low-voltage distribution test system in Thailand was conducted on Digsilent Powerfactory software. The results show that the hybrid linear and binary search method can improve the precision of the Monte Carlo-based method compared to the linear method. Finally, when the locational PV installed capacities are weighted by their peak locational load, the calculated PVHC significantly decreases.

articleTitle: Enhancing THAI Image Captioning Performance using CNN and Bidirectional LSTM
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: This research has designed a deep learning model to create Thai captions using a convolutional neural network (CNN) in VGG16 format to extract image features, and it is used to procreate captions using bidirectional LSTM. The data warehouse used for training and testing is Flickr8k, which combines customized traffic-related image and caption information. For the first set of data, that is Flickr8k, all subtitles had to be translated from English to Thai using Google Translate, and ways to deal with the data before training were to remove special characters to prevent the Thai language description from being distorted. Then, to evaluate the result of the captions the model produced compared to default captions, the BLEU metric was used to measure the score. The resulting average score was effective because it was higher than the compared models. The score values were paralleled up to 4 grams.

articleTitle: Real Time Distribution Grid Visualization using Smart Meters
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: The electric distribution system today is seeing the rapid integration of different new technologies such as electric vehicles and Distributed Energy Resources which can all severely degrade its effectiveness such as reduced line hosting capacity, poor voltage quality etc. The real-time monitoring of the distribution grid will allow for better decision making for distribution system operator thus helping to improve the situation with the real time information of the grid. This paper proposes a methodology for real time visualization of grid where the data from smart sensors are collected which are located at domestic loads, transformer and roof top photovoltaics and then transferred to an electrical software containing model of distribution system under study; Power flow analysis is then performed in the software to calculate different monitoring variables such as line hosting capacity, nodal voltage and power losses. The system is implemented and tested for the distribution system of Kathmandu University. The field result show that the proposed method can provide the grid status in an efficient manner.

articleTitle: LVDT Read-Out Circuit Based on Modified Wien Bridge Oscillator
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: This paper presents the LVDT Read-Out Circuit based on the Modified Wien Bridge Oscillator. The proposed read-out circuit converts inductance from LVDT to frequency output and does not need compensation circuits for primary to secondary phase shifts. The basic structure of the read-out circuit consists of a modified Wien bridge oscillator, a Level shift circuit, a comparator circuit, and a frequency counter (Atmega328p). The ratio metric method is used for linearity. The experiments show that it effectively enhances the LVDT linearity range, with linearity errors below 20%.

articleTitle: On Solving Area Coverage for Heterogeneous Directional Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: Wireless sensor networks play important roles in the intelligent systems of current technology, such as the Internet of Things (IoT). The heterogeneous directional sensor network (HDSN), which contains a large number of sensor nodes with different capabilities and is limited in sensing direction, has become more realistic in many applications.
