However, most existing works in the literature focus on homogeneous and omni-directional sensor networks, which cannot be efficiently applied to real-world applications. Therefore, in this study, we propose a novel algorithm called the Van der Waals Force-Based Algorithm for Heterogeneous Directional Sensor Networks (VW-HDSN) to solve the coverage problem in HDSNs. The simulation results illustrate that our algorithm can achieve a superior coverage ratio compared to that of a random approach by 18.66%. The results also suggest that adding efficient nodes to the network will significantly improve its performance. Another benefit of our algorithm is that it can be generalized to a fully heterogeneous network where all nodes are diverse in angle of view and sensing radius.

articleTitle: Energy Storage Valuation toward 100% Renewable Electricity from Reliability Perspective
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: Resource adequacy ensures reliable operation of energy grid. The analysis focuses on how each resource can contribute firm capacity value to the system. With renewable energy sources where the energy produced are highly variable and uncertain, such capacity value needs to be determined. Various power utilities around the world utilize a concept of Effective Load Carrying Capacity (ELCC) to estimate capacity value of renewable energy sources. This paper proposes a simplified deterministic approach to quantify benefits of energy storage to improve capacity value with high penetration of renewable energy sources.

articleTitle: Scaling Error Verification of DCC Bridges 6010C and 6020Q
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: For measuring the standard resistors in the intermedia range of 1Ω to 10 kΩ using the commercial Direct Current Comparator (DCC) bridges model 6010C and 6020Qthe scaling error of the DCC bridges should be investigated. This work proposes the verification by using the known values of the standard resistors with the resistance ratios of 1:1 and 10:1, which have very high stability in the controlled environment of temperature within (23.00 ± 0.05) °C during measurement. The scaling error can be estimated from the difference between the calculated resistance ratio and the measured resistance ratio. Comparison results of 6010C and 6020Q show the consistency of the resistance measurement ratios. Both DCC bridges give compatible results with their manufacturer's specification in 0.05 μΩ/Ω and 0.015 μΩ/Ω for model 6010C and 6020Q, respectively. With the proposed validation method, the scaling error of the DCC bridge is at a level of 10–<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</sup> μΩ/Ω.

articleTitle: Transparent UHF-RFID Tag Antenna for IoT Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: In this paper, a transparent UHF-RFID tag antenna is proposed for seamless integration into smart city IoT applications. The antenna features a transparent radiator made from an Indium Tin Oxide (ITO) conductive film on a glass substrate. The antenna design incorporates a loop structure with a meander line and a T-matching network to match the input impedance of the RFID chip. CST Microwave Studio was used to simulate the antenna performance. A parametric study was conducted to optimize the design and analyze the antenna performance based on different properties of the glass substrate and the ITO film. The proposed RFID tag antenna is designed on a 3mm thick Corning 0080 glass substrate and exhibits a radiation efficiency of 37% with a gain of -2.10dBi. The relatively low radiation efficiency is caused by the high dielectric loss of the glass substrate and the high conductive loss of the ITO film. The proposed design aims for the best possible efficiency of a transparent RFID tag antenna despite the high loss of the materials. Compared to a conventional RFID tag, the proposed transparent tag offers seamless integration with architectural glass structures in smart buildings at the cost of a lower read range. With the length of 0.20 λ<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$o$</tex>,the proposed tag antenna is considered electrically small.

articleTitle: A Planar Non-Destructive Glass Thickness Sensor Based on Capacitance Measurement
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: This article introduces a capacitive sensor for measuring glass thickness from 3 mm to 19 mm. The design, featuring two electrode fingers on FR4 substrate, undergoes iterative optimization to achieve optimal dimensional parameters. Experiments focus on tuning the electrode fingers' width and gap for sensitivity. Simulated capacitance values with different glass thickness demonstrate the sensor's capability in distinguishing the thickness of the glass samples. Precise tuning steps and parameter adjustments for enhanced sensing performance are described. This study offers insights into capacitive sensors for glass thickness measurement including the effects of geometric parameters of the electrodes and variation of the substrate materials.

articleTitle: Experience NECTEC's Virtual 3D Mini-Exhibition Hall: A Digital Showcase for Online Visitors
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: This study proposes a novel way to improve the online visitor experience at the National Electronics and Computer Technology Center (NECTEC) by providing virtual access to its mini exhibit space and facilities. To enable visitors to explore from a first-person perspective, the main goal is to transform NECTEC's vast 2D indoor location system into an immersive 3D world. Using Unity, a desktop program communicates in realtime with NECTEC's indoor location database to let users find the shortest route to designated locations inside the virtual environment. Furthermore, the study explores sophisticated functionalities like customized avatar tracking and interior navigation. The system is unique because it can dynamically customize avatars using uploaded photos, enabling customized tracking experiences. This study shows that combining virtual environments with real-world indoor location systems is feasible and can improve visitor engagement and interaction through testing and implementation.

articleTitle: Investigation and Modeling of Solar PV: A Simulation Method
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: Combining solar photovoltaic panels with pre-existing buildings may be a workable way to reduce carbon emissions and address the present energy issue. The purpose of this project is to create an energy-harvesting system that can assist nations like Bangladesh in meeting their energy needs while lowering their carbon footprint and forgoing the need for extra resources. This will be accomplished by utilizing three software tools (PVSOL, PVsyst, and SAM) that are tailored for various installations. One of Bangladesh's longest bridges, the Bangabandhu Bridge, underwent computer-aided design, modeling, and simulation of a mono-facial solar panel-based energy model in a sustainable manner. To obtain a more comprehensive understanding of the system's effectiveness, a thorough energy analysis was conducted. Based on our findings, we conclude that there is a great deal of promise for this endeavor. The average energy yield, according to the statistics, is 2948512kWh year. In the event of an energy crisis, this dependable energy can be used to power the entire bridge and the national grid.

articleTitle: Development and Evaluation of a Wireless System for Remote Monitoring of Rumen Temperature in Dairy Cows
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: This paper presents a wireless monitoring system designed for remotely tracking the rumen temperature of dairy cows. The system utilizes commercially available RF and LoRa modules, enabling the transmission of temperature data from within the cow to external IoT devices. Both modules operate on the 433 MHz frequency. From measured results, the received signal strength indicator (RSSI) values range between -80 to -90 dBm at pillar positions. Along the cow's body, the RSSI values fall within the range of -67 to -80 dBm. Additionally, signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) values along the cow's body exhibit improvement compared to those along the pillow, showing a difference of 2 to 4 dB within the 0 to 10 dB range. Importantly, LoRa offers a significant advantage over RF in terms of transmission range, reaching up to 5 meters compared to 2.5 meters for RF module, making it suitable for both indoor and outdoor farm environments. This system has the potential to revolutionize smart livestock monitoring by providing a non-invasive and efficient way to track the health of dairy cows.

articleTitle: A Sparse Quadratic Programming Approach to Supervisory Control of Multi-Zone HVAC Systems with Consideration of Peak Demand Shaving and Thermal Comfort
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: The HVAC system is one of the major power consuming equipment in buildings. Considering the effective setpoint temperature of each zone can increase efficiency in managing power usage in buildings, leading to the operating cost reduction. This paper presents the design of supervisory control (SC) for multi-zone HVAC systems that aims to minimize the total operating cost (TOC) and the thermal comfort cost (TCC). To minimize the TOC and TCC, both objectives are normalized and combined as a quadratic programming (QP) problem which can be efficiently solved. To achieve the design objective, two methods of SC are developed for multi-zone, namely, centralized SC and decentralized SC. We apply standard QP and sparse QP solvers using interior point method. The numerical results reveal that centralized SC performs better according to a tradeoff curve which TOC and TCC are lower. While both solvers give the same results, sparse solver can provide the solutions faster than interior point method. This paper demonstrates that centralized control is appropriate for implementation in multi-zones buildings and the sparse solver proves to be more suitable in the context of sparse QP problem.

articleTitle: FMCW Radar-Based Enhancing Moving Target Positioning Accuracy in Spectrogram Mapping
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a methodology aimed to enhancing the accuracy of moving target positioning using FMCW radar within spectrogram mapping. Utilizing a 10 GHz operating frequency, the FMCW radar effectively detects moving targets. However, the interpretation of intermediate frequency (IF) signals posed challenges due to multiple reflections and resulting ambiguous distances between objects. For solving this problem, we propose two steps of solution: employing an enveloping method and normalization of the IF signal. This process can extract maximum amplitude peaks specific to the target. Experimental validation involved detecting a drone moving away from the radar. Comparative analysis pre and post signal processing in spectrogram terms demonstrate the efficacy of our technique. Furthermore, verification of the detection range of radar was conducted using the GSM-015 GNSS speed meter. Results confirm the accuracy of the positioning capabilities of radar, emphasizing the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Power Management Control Strategy Based On Fuzzy Logic Algorithm for Parallel Boost High Gain Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: The parallel connection of modules is a commonly used technique to increase the power rating of a power converter. However, this approach can have significant drawbacks in terms of impact on load, safety, and reliability. Therefore, the converter architecture and control must be designed with flexibility to ensure operation. This paper proposes a novel power management control strategy based on fuzzy logic algorithms. The proposed method is applied to manage the output power between parallel boost high gain converter. The power management conditions of each module depend on the output power that the load requires. Moreover, the power management system is also designed to provide support if one of the three modules fails. The considered system consists of three parallel converter modules rated at 375 W. Simulation with MATLAB/Simulink was used to evaluate the performance of the proposed method. The simulation results show that the output power of each module can be effectively managed according to the load demand.

articleTitle: Low-Cost Sky Camera with Centralized Storage Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: Sky cameras play a pivotal role in very short-term irradiance forecasting. However, the existing sky camera solutions available in the market are prohibitively expensive. In this paper, a low-cost sky camera using Closed-Circuit Television (CCTV) cameras with centralized storage systems is proposed and the prototype has been developed. By including CCTV cameras, L2TP/IPsec VPN connections, and storage systems, the prototype low-cost sky camera can be achieved at a cost of approximately 160 USD per unit. During the 245-day testing period, the sky images captured at everyone-minute interval are successfully stored in the centralized storage systems. Future design considerations include camera sensor lifetime and how to prevent storage run out of space.

articleTitle: Study of Machine Learning Algorithms for Detecting Web Bot
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: Nowadays, automation software systems play a crucial role in assisting humans with specific tasks, particularly in online communication for timely interactions. However, the misuse of such systems poses risks, impacting website performance, leading to data access violations, or even posing threats to the system's security. To address these challenges, an automatic software inspection system has been developed as a prototype, aimed at preventing potential issues in the online domain. Machine learning algorithms are employed to enhance detection accuracy, with the decision tree algorithm demonstrating a maximum accuracy of 97.4%. This promising result suggests its suitability for further development into a JavaScript library, offering a valuable resource for future website applications.

articleTitle: Tunable Pendulum Energy Harvester Using Cone Continuously Variable Transmission
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: This paper proposes a tunable pendulum energy harvesting system incorporating a Cone Continuous Variable Transmission (Cone CVT) design. The goal is to build upon the resonance state observed in previous adaptive-tuned vibration absorber research by integrating a converter to transform mechanical energy into electrical energy. The system dynamically tunes itself in response to varying excitation frequencies. In this design, a Cone CVT is installed between the pendulum stem and the dynamo. Additionally, a conventional PID controller is employed to adjust the wheel position. A mathematical model is developed to predict system response and performance for different design parameters. MATLAB ODE45 and ODE23 solvers are utilized for simulation, generating data for dynamic system analysis. The analytical model is validated by tuning the frequency within the range of 1 to 5.24 rad/s. The outcomes demonstrate that, following the tuning algorithm, the pendulum enters a resonance state, leading to a significant increase in output voltage, approximately 10 times compared to the initial value.

articleTitle: Clustering of Ionospheric Irregularities based on Spatiotemporal ROTI Keogram Images
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: Ionospheric irregularities associated with Equatorial plasma bubbles (EPB) can significantly impact navigation and communication systems. Therefore, their occurrences need to be studied and predicted. To solve the prediction problem, it is necessary to identify types of spatiotemporal characteristics as reference points for the predictive model. This work employs unsupervised machine learning algorithms to identify types of ionospheric irregularities due to EPB using the rate of total electron content index (ROTI) keograms. Two machine learning methods: two models, the Gaussian mixture model (GMM), and k-means, are considered. Comparative analysis is performed, and the optimal number of clusters is estimated using one classical, k-means and one additional - repeatability score, introduced in this work metric. The optimal GMM model successfully classifies three types of irregularity patterns offering valuable insights for the development of an effective EPB prediction model and enhancing our understanding of ionospheric behavior.

articleTitle: A Modified Super-Twisting Sliding-Mode Control for Reducing Robot Arm Dynamic Vibration
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: The main challenges in controlling robot arms in rescue robots or robotic-assisted surgery are dynamic vibration and overshoot. This paper introduces a new technique to address these issues. To validate the control performance of the proposed technique, it is compared with other control strategies. A BLDC motor drive module, equipped with BLDC motors, has been developed to evaluate three different speed control techniques for a robot arm. Among the three control techniques tested, conventional PI control reaches the set point but exhibits high dynamic vibration, high overshoot, and poor tracking performance. This issue was mitigated by using Super-Twisting Sliding-Mode Control (ST-SMC), which reduces dynamic vibration but still results in high overshoot. Consequently, the proposed controller, named Modified Super-Twisting Sliding-Mode Control (MST-SMC), was developed to address the overshoot problem associated with ST-SMC while retaining the benefit of reduced dynamic vibration. The test results conclusively demonstrate that MST-SMC delivers the best performance, characterized by low amplitude of vibration, minimal overshoot, and the shortest settling times. Additionally, it achieves superior tracking performance.

articleTitle: Robust Flux-Weakening Control Approach for Three-Phase Induction Motor Drives
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: A robust flux-weakening control strategy for induction motor drives is presented in this article. The voltage feedback part, which is the difference in amplitude between the command voltage and the voltage limit, is utilized to enhance the tracking accuracy of the weakening current rather than using only the feedforward control as the conventional method. The limitation of the maximum q-axis current is adapted in any flux-weakening region. The maximum torque per ampere (MTPA) trajectory is implemented in the constant torque region in order to achieve the maximum torque. Likewise, the maximum slip speed can be obtained based on the optimal current condition in the flux-weakening region II, in which cannot accessible by the conventional method. Indeed, the proposed method provides a reduction of the rotor flux appropriately to the increased speed in the flux-weakening regions under the controllable operation, resulting in a robust control strategy. The effectiveness of the proposed method is confirmed by simulation results.

articleTitle: A Simple Chaos-Based Compressed Sensing with Encryption Scheme for Wearable IoT Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: As an advancement of Internet-of-Thing (IoT) technology, wearable devices have become increasingly prevalent. However, ensuring the safety of the data and managing power consumption are crucial issue. This paper presents an integration of compressed sensing and encryption scheme for wearable IoT devices. The advantages of compressed sensing (CS) and chaotic system are integrated, i.e., reducing data transmission and storage requirements and concurrently enhancing the security and randomness of the encryption process. A 1-dimensional signum-based piecewise-linear chaotic map is utilized as a source of random sensing and robust key generation for the encryption. While the sparse measurement matrix effectively reduces the dimensionality of the data. The security and compressive capability are demonstrated through FitBit Fitness Tracker dataset, in terms of compression ratio, reconstruction quality, statistical analysis and security analysis. The results show that the scheme can achieve high compression and encryption efficiency, while facilitating transmission band-width without compromising quality of the information. The proposed system ensures minimal computational overhead and enable energy-saving feature that can be easily implemented to various types of wearable technologies.

articleTitle: A Novel CCCCTA-Based High Frequency Memristor Emulator in 180 nm CMOS Technology Process
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: In this article, we introduce a novel Memristor Emulator (MRE) model employing a single analog building block i.e., the Current Controlled Current Conveyor Transconductance Amplifier (CCCCTA), along with two resistors and one capacitor. We further show the operation of the proposed MRE in both grounded as well as floating modes. The proposed MRE operates up to 1 MHz. In addition, by using a simple switch connection, the proposed emulator circuit works in both incremental as well as decremental configuration. The simulation results are based on a 1.1 V power supply and have been carried out on a 180 nm CMOS technology node. The results perfectly corroborate the theoretical propositions. Besides, the design incurs a power consumption of only 2.2 mW. Such low power design of the proposed MRE can be exploited for various energy-efficient applications.

articleTitle: Development of VOCs Mixture Biomarker Classification System Based on Preconcentrator with Embedded Sensing Control
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: A volatile organic compound (VOCs) classification system is developed for non-invasive biomarker screening tests. The developed system utilizes a preconcentrator, which contains an absorbent material for trapping VOCs at low temperatures and thermally desorbing at specific elevated temperatures. This system is especially useful for detection of odor mixture at low concentration and target VOCs biomarkers in the odor sample can also be measured with enhanced selectivity. All sensing processes, including a PID temperature controller for heating preconcentrator, odor sensor interface, and solenoid valve control, are performed using only a single embedded microcontroller. An odor mixture with low concentration is measured and classified in order to investigate the developed system. The result of the experiment and the principal component analysis (PCA) shows that the system with the preconcentrator can measure the VOCs mixture of odor sample in terms of sensitivity and selectivity. This system prototype is useful for screening tests of exhaled breath biomarker.

articleTitle: Effect of Limited Number of RF Chains and Training Power on Massive MIMO Downlink
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: We investigate how the number of radio frequency (RF) chains and the training power for channel estimation affect the sum-achievable rate in the massive MIMO downlink. With a limited number of RF chains, the base station (BS) applies hybrid combining to estimate the channel on the uplink and hybrid precoding to transmit data signals on the downlink. For limited training power, the number of RF chains can be much fewer than the number of antennas. Our simulation shows that with limited training power, the BS can employ only 16 RF chains for 64 BS antennas and 4 user equipments to achieve the maximal sum rate.

articleTitle: Monitoring Air Conditioner Malfunctions Using Power Consumption and Temperature
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: This paper suggests a method for monitoring air conditioner malfunctions through the analysis of power consumption and temperature. The approach involves utilizing an electric meter connected to the circuit that supplies the air conditioner, ensuring a non-intrusive setup. The meter records voltage-current values for the AC, which are then used to calculate power consumption. Additionally, room temperature is measured using a thermal couple. Subsequently, an experimental assessment of the air conditioner's condition is performed by activating the compressor for testing. Measurements are taken for both temperature and the aggregate electrical circuit that supplies power. The experimental results concerning air conditioner malfunction monitoring demonstrate distinct differences in the timing of power consumption on the compressor and off, as well as variations in temperature increase and decrease.

articleTitle: A Robust Approach to COVID-19 CT-Scan Image Denoising with Inception Residual Attention UNET
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: A CT scan is crucial for evaluating the severity of a COVID-19 infection; however, exposure to radiation can increase the risk of developing cancer. To mitigate this risk, the intensity of radiation is significantly reduced, though it comes at the cost of introducing noise in the CT images. UNET has gained immense popularity in medical image denoising, but as the depth of the network increases, performance begins to degrade. In this paper, a novel UNET-based architecture named Inception Residual Attention UNET (IRAUNET) for denoising single and mixed-noise CT-scan images is proposed. The improvements in existing U-Nets are as follows: (1) IRAUNET employs residual blocks to enhance the depth of the network, preventing degradation issues. (2) The proposed network introduces an inception mechanism in the residual block, allowing multi-scale feature extraction and increasing adaptability to distinct noise patterns. (3) The proposed network incorporates an attention mechanism within skip connections to refine image feature extraction and selectively preserve crucial details. Compared to seven established models commonly used for image denoising, IRAUNET exhibits substantial advancements, leading to superior numerical and qualitative outcomes.

articleTitle: Emotion Detection from Electroencephalography Signals Using String Grammar K-Nearest Neighbors
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) signals-based motion detection has become more popular recently. There are several methods proposed to ease this application. However, in this paper, we apply a different approach, i.e., we explore the syntactic approach in detecting emotion from the EEG signals. In particular, we develop a translation method to translate an EEG signal into a string. Then we utilize the string grammar <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k{-}$</tex> NN method to find a suitable class for each test signal. However, since it is a string calculation, we have to use the Levenshtein distance instead of a regular distance calculation. From the validation test results, we found that the maximum accuracy rate is 96.95% in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$4^{\text{th}}$</tex> validation with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k=3$</tex>. For the test results with the same model, we found that the accuracy rate is around 87 - 89%. This shows that this syntactic pattern recognition can provide comparable results with existing methods.

articleTitle: Learning-Based Locomotion Controllers for Quadruped Robots in Indoor Stair Climbing via Deep Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: This paper introduces a learning-based locomotion controller for quadruped robots, employing Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) to enhance stair climbing capabilities in indoor settings. This approach combines a detailed locomotion controller specifically designed for navigating stairs. It also utilizes a comprehensive observation space that aids in the informed execution of terrain height information and movements. The core of this research lies in the development of a controller that achieves speeds of 1 m/s, with notable success rates of 90% and 98% for staircase configurations. This achievement demonstrates how the controller could significantly improve the adaptability and efficiency of quadruped robots in complex environments, paving the way for wider applications in challenging environments.

articleTitle: Experimental Analysis of Aged XLPE Cable Using Return Voltage Measurement
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: XLPE cables are widely used for underground power transmission and distribution. Therefore, condition assessment of cable insulation is important. In this work, Return Voltage Measurement (RVM) is carried out to diagnose and characterise temperature - humidity aged XLPE cable insulation. The XLPE insulation is aged under constant stress and cyclic stress. The effect of both temperature and humidity is considered while ageing the samples. It is observed that return voltage characteristics change with ageing conditions. The measured parameters i.e. maximum return voltage, time to reach maximum return voltage and slope of the rise of return voltage are recorded. The calculated parameters i.e. p - factor and reliability factor are obtained using MATLAB curve fitting tool. Both the measured and calculated parameters is seen to change with ageing conditions. With ageing, the parameter values decrease compared to unaged XLPE. Therefore, the measured and calculated parameters can be used as ageing marker. Also, it is observed that percentage of relative humidity plays an important role on ageing.

articleTitle: Temporal Analysis of ECG Characteristics for Predicting Defibrillation Success in Ventricular Fibrillation During Resuscitation
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: This paper reports a study for predicting defibrillation outcomes in Ventricular Fibrillation (VF) patients through the analysis of ECG signals. A dataset of 251 sudden cardiac arrest cases underwent ECG recording, and time-domain features were extracted from pre-shock signals. The dataset was classified into successful (ROEA) and unsuccessful (NoROEA) shock outcomes, employing Gaussian Naive Bayes, K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), and Support Vector Machine (SVM) models. Statistical analysis revealed significant differences in all studied features between ROEA and NoROEA groups. The Gaussian Naive Bayes model exhibited the highest accuracy (81.33% in the test set) and was recommended for predicting shock outcomes. Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) curve analysis indicated fair discriminatory performance (AUC: 0.7956) for the Gaussian Naive Bayes model.

articleTitle: Impacts of Electric Vehicle Charging on Residential Feeders
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: The global shift towards electric vehicles (EVs) is marked as a significant transformation towards transportation industry, driven by the urgent necessity to curb carbon emissions and address climate change concerns. Electric vehicles are widely regarded as environmentally friendly due to their zero-emission operation. However, the integration of electric vehicles into the power grid presents intricate challenges that require thorough examination. When multiple electric vehicles are charging simultaneously, the local power system has an abrupt surge in electricity demand. This surge results in voltage problems, overloads, and increased power losses. The vulnerability of the home grid segment is particularly pronounced during peak charging hours. The primary objective of this study is to conduct a comprehensive assessment of the impact of EV charging on the electricity grid. This paper involves simulating the operation of a MATLAB-based 13-node system and analyzing the effects of EV charging on voltage, and system performance. The study seeks to offer information on the impacts of EV adoption on local electrical infrastructure. With the growing number of electric vehicles on the roads, it becomes increasingly imperative to devise solutions that ensure the reliability of the local power system. This research aims to contribute to the development of strategies for the secure and efficient connection of EVs to the grid, promoting a more sustainable and dependable energy future.

articleTitle: Experimental results on FMCW radar based Human Recognition using only Doppler information
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: The demand of indoor human identification systems that prioritize privacy has led to an increased interest in wireless sensing devices such as radar. Several studies have identified distinctive characteristics of human movement that cause Doppler signatures, which can be used for subject identification. Following them, this paper proposes an alternative machine learning approach for human identification, which uses only Doppler information from each subject by using FMCW radar. Experimental results in the two-subject scenarios show that the proposed method can achieve an accuracy of 96.2% (±1.1%) when data for both training and verification are obtained from the same scenarios, while an accuracy of 67.0% (±2.8<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>) can be achieved when data for the verification are obtained from different scenarios

articleTitle: Analysis, Design and Implementation of Class-E Inverter for Wireless Charging Application
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: This paper extensively investigates the analysis, design, and practical implementation of a class E resonant inverter with zero voltage switching (ZVS) capabilities, specifically tailored for wireless charging applications. The equivalent circuit of the Class E inverter utilized in wireless power transfer is thoroughly examined to derive the requisite formulas. The modes of operation were thoroughly analyzed by studying the corresponding waveforms. Based on the derived formulas, the circuit parameters were calculated. To validate the proposed design, a prototype of the wireless power transfer system was developed. Both simulation results and experimental findings confirmed the successful transfer of wireless power, achieving the desired output power. Additionally, it was observed that the power switch can operate under ZVS condition for horizontal misalignments within the range of 0–18 mm and a vertical distance between the coupled coils of 5 mm.

articleTitle: Current Control Design Based on Dynamic Model of Vienna Rectifier for Harmonic Mitigation
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: The Vienna Rectifier is an AC-DC converter system with features that allow for a high output voltage and minimal ripple compared to a conventional rectifier that does not draw current from the grid. The main differences between conventional and Vienna rectifiers are harmonics, power factor, and efficiency. The Vienna rectifier reduces grid-side harmonics and improves the power factor. In this research, the current in the Q-axis is controlled to zero so that the power factor of the system is as close to one as possible, and a PI controller is used to create a stable output signal for the system. The result is that the system can produce an output voltage level of 800V and a THD of less than 5%, according to IEEE 519–2022 standards. The efficiency of the input signal has been improved, which can reduce the THD of the input as well. The research also tested software designed with C2000 microcontrollers to prove that the designed model can operate in real-life situations.

articleTitle: Set-Membership Orthogonal Gradient Adaptive Algorithm on Least Mean Fourth Criterion
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: In this paper, we introduce a set-membership mechanism on the orthogonal gradient adaptive (OGA) algorithm based on least mean fourth (LMF) algorithm. In accordance with the fast convergence, the OG A-based scheme is conducted based on LMF algorithm that is described with the fourth power of the estimated error. The organisation of proposed algorithm composes with a brief of set-membership adaptive filtering and taking an advantage of OGA algorithm based on LMF algorithm. In order to make a smooth, an adaptive learning rate of algorithm and threshold value are furnished for convergence rate performance. There are some experimental simulations from proposed algorithm that show the mean square error trends can converge remarkably to the existing algorithm for system identification.

articleTitle: Water Pumping System Using DC Motor Pump with Full Bridge Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: This research proposes the creation of a DC - DC converter to supply DC voltage to DC motors for pumping. The circuit has a DC bus voltage of 24 volts using the MBB50BS6 IGBT Module. Unipolar PWM Full Bridge Converter with TMS320F28379D can adjust the duty cycle from 0.1 - 1.0, allowing the voltage to be adjusted from 2.4 - 24 volts. The motor consumes current from 1.04 - 7.13 amperes. The speed of the pump motor is adjusted from 306 - 3,590 rpm. Pumping water volume from 1.53 - 33.48 liters per minute.

articleTitle: Design and Experimentation of CP Sequential-Rotated Patch Antenna for Nanosatellite Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: This paper proposes a circularly polarized (CP) sequential-rotated patch antenna for nanosatellite communication systems. The proposed CP sequential-rotated patch antenna comprised of 2 × 2 corner-truncated rectangular patch with a slot, and sequentially rotated feeding (SRF). The SRF was used to improve impedance matching and CP bandwidth. These patches and SRF were fabricated on Rogers 5880 substrate. Moreover, this antenna was integrated with radome and enclosures for space environment hazards. The measured results at 2.1 GHz (center frequency) achieved RLBW of 73.33% (1.46 - 3 GHz) and ARBW of 23.33% (1.87 - 2.36 GHz). The optimal gain (RHCP) was 5 dBic at 2.25 GHz with bi-directional radiation, rendering the proposed antenna suitable for S-band nanosatellite technology.

articleTitle: Development of an Autoscan Motorized Microscope Utilizing the OpenFlexure Architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: This paper presents the design, development, and implementation of an autoscan motorized microscope based on the OpenFlexure Architecture-a modular and cost-effective platform for motorized microscopy. To achieve high-quality specimen imaging, traditional methodologies often require manual manipulation of the specimen along the X-Y-Z axes by a specialist. In enhancing the OpenFlexure platform, our modification introduces automated scan and autofocus features. This augmentation facilitates efficient specimen scanning, reducing dependency on manual manipulation and advancing the capabilities of the architecture. By mitigating the vignette issue, utilizing a multi-extended depth of field, and incorporating photo stitching, the experimental results substantiate the system's capacity to generate a large autofocus image from 11x11 photos in under 10 minutes. These outcomes underscore its potential for a broad spectrum of scientific and medical applications.

articleTitle: EEG-based Brain-Computer Interface System via Time-Locked Visual Attention for Assistive Device Control
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: This work proposes a brain-computer interface system using visual attention paradigm. We used count-down numbers for different periods of attention to command creation from EEG signals. Electrode positions and feature extraction algorithm were verified. By using four number and the proposed simple classification method can produce four commands. The results showed that EEG from the occipital region using an alpha-beta ratio achieved an average classification accuracy of 80. 56% and 62.06% for two and four commands, respectively. The proposed system can be used for severely physically disabled people for control and communication in the future. However, the proposed needs to improve for higher efficiency by session training and using complex algorithms and classifiers.

articleTitle: Fault Signals Reconstruct for Hand Kinematic Measurement Based on Compressed Sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: The measurement of hand kinematics is typically achieved through various approaches, such as data gloves, multiple cameras and optical trackers. These methods find applications in diverse fields, including 3D modeling, robotics, rehabilitation, and physiotherapy. However, each approach necessitates a significant number of sensors for accurate hand kinematic measurement. Data gloves, in particular, are prone to calibration issues, and they may encounter missing information due to fault sensors. Defects in these sensors can lead to safety and accuracy issues, especially in the context of using hand kinematics to control robots, particularly in remote surgery as shown that hand kinematic reconstruction is significant to enhance the efficiency and accuracy of hand kinematic analysis across various applications. This paper focuses on hand kinematic signals reconstruction from fault sensors using only measured signals, employing a compressed sensing technique. The proposed sparse sensor placement technique aims to reconstruct all fault signals with suitable accuracy by utilizing measured signals. To evaluate the performance of proposed methods, The Percentage Root-Mean-Square Difference (PRD) used to compare reconstructed signals with ground truth. The results of average PRD shown that the number of faulty sensors directly affects the quality of the reconstruction. As the number of faulty sensors increases, the performance of the reconstruction tends to decrease.

articleTitle: Deep learning-based Mango Fruit Detection and Counting
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: Mango is an agricultural product that is of important economic significance in Thailand, requiring yield estimation in order to plan for the harvest stage effectively. This research presents Mango fruit detection and counting on a canopy tree using a deep learning-based object detection model, Mask R-CNN and Cascade R-CNN. To acquire an image of a mango tree in the current circumstances, partial occlusion of mangoes usually occurs. We enhance the model learning by combining the Random Erasing method for image augmentation to improve performance in dealing with partial occlusion issues. This paper compares the performance of the different backbone layer for feature extraction. We utilize the most optimal backbone, RestNext-101-32x8d-FPN is an essential component of the model. The Mask R-CNN with Random Erasing outperforms the Cascade R-CNN achieving the highest performance with a precision score of 0.922, a recall score of 0.786, an F1-score of 0.849, a mAP@50 score of 0.883, and counting performance MAE score of 1.106 fruits per image. The best model can be deployed in real-world applications.

articleTitle: Coherent Detection Using SMF-Coupled LED with a Polarization-Insensitive Self-Homodyne Receiver
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: We demonstrate 10, 20, 30 GBaud QPSK and 5 GBaud 16QAM using an SMF-coupled LED and our self-homodyne receiver. The optimized LED's bandwidths are 0.7 nm for 10 & 20 GBaud QPSK and 0.9 nm for 30 GBaud QPSK & 5 GBaud 16QAM. The Q-factor with LED's bandwidth above 0.5 nm in all cases can reach the 25% overhead SD-FEC threshold.

articleTitle: Design of 3D-Cooling System of 100 kVA/22 kV Distribution Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: This paper presents the design of 3D-cooling system of 100 kVA/22 kV distribution transformer that utilizes the liquid insulation of the transformer. It will be ascertained the temperature rise, which is regarded as a difficulty in cooling system design due to the internal insulation values of transformer. The temperature relationship that exists inside the transformer will be determined using the transformer design guidelines in order to design a cooling system under the following conditions: the temperature rise of the upper oil shall not exceed 50°C, the temperature rise of the winding shall not exceed 55°C, and the ambient temperature shall not exceed 50°C. This paper will evaluate the temperature accuracy by comparing the estimated values with the test results using the IEC 60076–2 standard. As the results, the percentage can be obtained using the following formula, where each temperature measurement point has a unique calculated value: The differences in the average HV winding temperature rise of 7%, average winding temperature rise of 5%, and top oil temperature rise of 39% are all significant.

articleTitle: Antagonistic Parallel Elastic Actuator Using Preloaded Composite Spiral Torsion Springs
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: Parallel elastic actuators (PEA) are widely applied for robotic applications with asymmetric load requirement. The elastic components are included in the systems aiming to reduce the actuation peak torque required from the electric motors. However, higher torque may be required during the opposite motion. The fused deposition modeling technique allows fabrication of 3D printed composite spiral torsion springs for compact modular PEAs. The antagonistic design enables using the springs to support moment in bidirectional. Preloading is substantially required to ensure the winding deformation of both springs. The design of spring stiffness and equilibrium is the major challenge to minimize the actuation peak torque and power consumption. In this paper, the behavior of the parallel elastic actuator with preloaded springs while subjected to the pure stiffness load is observed in three cases: the PEA's spring has lower, higher, and the same stiffness as the load. The position and current of the brushless DC motor driven by the ODrive Pro motor controller are recorded. The experimental setup allows characterization of the spring component and the PEA using different number of spring stacks. The results of this study can be used as a reference for further designing of antagonistic PEAs with preload for asymmetric load support.

articleTitle: An Advanced Features Extraction Module for Remote Sensing Image Super-Resolution
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: In recent years, convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have achieved remarkable advancement in the field of remote sensing image super-resolution due to the complexity and variability of textures and structures in remote sensing images (RSIs), which often repeat in the same images but differ across others. Current deep learning-based super-resolution models focus less on high-frequency features, which leads to suboptimal performance in capturing contours, textures, and spatial information. State-of-the-art CNN-based methods now focus on the feature extraction of RSIs using attention mechanisms. However, these methods are still incapable of effectively identifying and utilizing key content attention signals in RSIs. To solve this problem, we proposed an advanced feature extraction module called Channel and Spatial Attention Feature Extraction (CSA-FE) for effectively extracting the features by using the channel and spatial attention incorporated with the standard vision transformer (ViT). The proposed method trained over the UCMerced dataset on scales 2, 3, and 4. The experimental results show that our proposed method helps the model focus on the specific channels and spatial locations containing high-frequency information so that the model can focus on relevant features and suppress irrelevant ones, which enhances the quality of super-resolved images. Our model achieved superior performance compared to various existing models.

articleTitle: Delayed WiFi Communications Feedback Control Primary-Side Buck Converter for CC-CV Inductive Wireless EV Charging
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: This paper aimed to study the delayed WiFi communications for constant current and constant voltage (CC-CV) inductive wireless EV charging coupled to the primary side (PS) buck converter through the ESP 32 feedback controllers on the secondary side (SS). The results show that the cascade PI controller achieved the transient response, non-steady state error, stability, and reliability for the wireless charging system with a delayed time feedback signal of 30 ms based on the step-resistance load and lithium battery charging for 20% to 90% SOC. Ultimately, the system's current and voltage gains produced cascade feedback signals from the SS and the primary side buck converter output, outperforming the battery unit's single-stage feedback current and voltage signals. The system achieved 88% efficiency during charging with 380 W to 800 W.

articleTitle: Automated Object Keypoints Dataset Generation Using Blender
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: This research paper explores the use of Blender, a powerful 3D computer software, as a convenient alternative to the traditional hand labeling method for generating keypoints datasets for object pose estimation. By leveraging Blender's capabilities and automating the generation of labeled keypoints data; this offers significant time and resource savings when compared to manual labeling, thereby reducing the workload of keypoints annotation. This study aims to compare the speed and model accuracy achieved by using the Blender-generated dataset against the conventional hand labeling approach. Through experimentation, the synthetic datasets generated from Blender demonstrated an accuracy that rivals traditionally hand-labeled datasets yet demanded a fraction of the time. Shortening the process of taking pictures and labeling keypoints of objects is desirable for manipulation tasks such as service robots set up in unknown environments.

articleTitle: Pioneering Simplicity in Computer Vision: A First-Hand Account of Developing a Low-Code OpenCV Interface for Defect Detection Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: In the pursuit of democratizing computer vision technology, this paper presents a first-hand account of the development of a low-code interface for OpenCV, a leading library in the field. Our research introduces a user-friendly platform that enables users with varying levels of programming expertise to effectively implement computer vision solutions. Recognizing the technical barriers presented by traditional hard coding, we have integrated a meticulous survey method designed to assess the effectiveness of the low-code interface for defect detection tasks within computer vision. Participants from diverse expertise levels-Beginners, Intermediates, and Experts-were provided with three defect detection use cases. They were tasked with identifying and delineating defects using both traditional OpenCV methods and our innovative low-code GUI and SDK, enabling a direct comparison of the two approaches in a controlled environment. By analyzing the development time and parameters tuning, we demonstrate significant reductions in implementation time across all levels of expertise. For hard code implementations, with Beginners reducing their development time from 39.4 minutes to just 5.9 minutes, Intermediates from 24.5 minutes to 3.4 minutes, and Experts from 9.1 minutes to a brisk 1.3 minutes. Moreover, parameter tuning-often a time-intensive process-also saw considerable time decreases, with Beginners' times dropping from 25.4 to 15.0 minutes, Intermediates from 18.0 to 10.0 minutes, and Experts from 10.2 to 5.3 minutes when using the low-code solution. These results underscore the potential of low-code platforms to significantly streamline the development process, simplifying complex tasks and offering a more inclusive and productive environment for developers of all levels. The findings advocate for a paradigm shift towards low-code platforms, especially in fields that demand rapid and agile development cycles like computer vision.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison of Convolutional and Transformer Neural Networks in Defect Classification for Industrial Images
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: In the semiconductor industry, the utilization of advanced visual inspection technology confronts challenges due to the scarcity of the defect data and the substantial sizes of the images involved, which pose difficulties for traditional Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). Most CNN techniques are evaluated on common resolutions, around 224 x 224 pixels, with limited literature available on their application to larger image resolutions, such as 1024 x 1024 pixels. Furthermore, the recent surge in popularity of transformer-based models, exemplified by Vision-Transformer (ViT), underscores the evolving landscape. However, ViT's efficacy, particularly with smaller datasets (less than 2000), has prompted the development of hybrid deep learning approaches like the Compact Convolutional Transformer (CCT), specifically build to address problems related to large data. Hence, in this study, we conduct a comparative performance evaluation among ResNet50, MobileNet-v2, and CCT aiming to assess their effectiveness in handling large size images and small datasets drawn from real-world semiconductor industry scenarios. Our findings reveal that all three methods demonstrate commendable predictive capabilities, achieving accuracies of (LED Dataset [Binary Class] - Resnet50: 99.75%, MobileNet-v2: 99.87%, CCT: 97.12%; PCB Dataset [Multi Class]: Resnet50: 94.79%, MobileNet-v2: 95.67%, CCT: 94.87%) when utilizing our limited dataset sourced from actual semiconductor industry settings and publicly available resources.

articleTitle: Obstacle Risk Assessment for Unmanned Surface Vehicle Using Camera and Lidar
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: This research aims to enhance vessel capabilities in assessing dynamically moving obstacles, such as floating debris and other vessels, by leveraging data from cameras and 3D Lidar sensors. YOLOv8 is trained to detect obstacles, with a specific focus o n s hip vessels. Point cloud processing is employed to identify clustered point clouds and match them with bounding boxes. The position obtained from the previous step is then utilized to estimate velocity using the Kalman filter. The system provides realtime information on the closest distance of approach and the remaining time before potential collisions occur. We use the remaining time before potential collisions occur to determine whether the obstacle is approaching or receding from us.

articleTitle: Gamification for Manufacturing (GfM) Towards Era Industry 5.0
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: Gamification has become a popular issue in recent years in various industries, including manufacturing. Gamification for Manufacturing, or GfM, has the ability to improve workers' psychological well-being while also increasing productivity. In the age of Industry 5.0, GfM is one of the best solutions for achieving the revolution's basic value, which is human-centric. However, there is currently a lack of research that describes how GfM is implemented in Industry 5.0. As a result, this research aims to determine the most successful element design and the benefits and obstacles of GfM implementation in Industry 5.0. An analytical analysis of the relevant paper was performed to suggest a framework for implementing GfM in Industry 5.0 based on three core values, including human-centric, sustainable, and resilient factors. Professionals and researchers are expected to use the framework and move the manufacturing sector into a new era.

articleTitle: A Distribution Use of System Charge Calculation for Solar Photovoltaic Systems in Thailand
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: With the Thai government aiming to supply renewable energy accounting for 30% of the country's energy consumption by 2037, the role of consumers is becoming prosumers. However, the energy generated by photovoltaic (PV) systems has an impact on the distribution system, which is managed by a distribution system operator (DSO). This paper proposes a method for calculating the distribution use of system (DUoS) charge, with a focus on the actual amount associated with the distribution system price in Thailand's electricity bill structure. The proposed method aims to accurately reflect DSO's recovery needs without negatively affecting consumers who install PV systems. The case studies are designed to compare the DUoS charge under time-of-use and progressive rates, considering scenarios related to PV system energy generation, load support, and energy flow into the distribution system. Through simulation results and discussion, this paper provides insights into determining the appropriate DUoS charge in the context of PV systems in Thailand, contributing to the efficient integration of PV systems while maintaining fairness and sustainability in Thailand's energy distribution.

articleTitle: High Performance Deep Learning GPR Feature Detector Model for Potash Mining
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: Ground Penetrating Radar (GPR) has been an essential nondestructive geophysical tool in Saskatchewan's potash mines for over six decades. This innovative technology, used in conjunction with an active boring machine, facilitates realtime data collection, particularly for imaging the immediate clay seam (414-clay seam) above the mine roof. Its reliability is demonstrated by the accuracy with which the roof beam thickness (mine roof to 414-clay seam) is interpreted in realtime, crucial for making informed safety decisions during mining operations. The imperative for a robust auto-picking algorithm tailored to handle complexities in potash mine GPR data is emphasized. The previously developed algorithm called the Clustered Ratio Derivative (CRD) algorithm, employing unsupervised machine learning for realtime GPR interpretation showcased promising results. However, the CRD algorithm faces limitations due to potential sensitivity to variations in input data, especially in the presence of noise or anomalies. Geological variations, such as the presence of “stray clays” within the roof beam, pose challenges to the algorithm's performance and accuracy. In response to these challenges, this paper proposes a novel deep learning-based algorithm leveraging two distinct Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) architectures. These CNNs are designed to navigate the intricacies of the GPR data pattern specific to potash mines. The presented results indicate promising levels of accuracy, with the new method achieving 95.4% accuracy in detecting the 414-clay seam and an average of 88% accuracy in finding “stray clays” seen in the dataset when compared to a geophysicist interpretation. The overall analysis suggests that this new approach has the potential to detect mining room roof features with a high degree of accuracy.

articleTitle: Interactive Learning Through the Metaverse and its Impact on Primary Education
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: The rise of the Metaverse, an immersive, three-dimensional digital environment, has been gradually transforming human-computer interaction. This paper focuses on exploring the potential of the Metaverse to improve learning through interactive games. The Metaverse serves as a dynamic platform for students to collaborate, explore and engage with. It enables educators to create interactive learning environments that amalgamate both physical and virtual spaces through technologies such as virtual reality, augmented reality, and artificial intelligence. These interactive games within the Metaverse foster critical thinking and problem-solving on top of making learning enjoyable. This paper discusses the development of educational environments within the metaverse, the integration of interactive games as well as their impact on learning outcomes and student engagement. The Metaverse poses a novel route towards effective education with this gamified approach. This study highlights the potential for the Metaverse to prepare students for the challenges inherent in this digital age by transforming traditional educational methods.

articleTitle: The Future of E-commerce: Creating Immersive Experiences in Live Streaming Commerce to Drive Consumers' Impulse Buying
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: Nowadays, the integration of live streaming and cutting-edge technologies, notably AR and AI technologies, has given rise to a revolutionary paradigm in the ever-evolving world of e-commerce, changing the way customers interact with products and make decisions about what they want to buy. Live streaming has evolved from an e-commerce tool used mostly for entertainment to an ever evolving and combining with sophisticated technologies that helps close the gap between online and offline shopping experiences. This study used immersive experience as a mediating variable based on the stimulus-organism-response (S-O-R) model. A structural equation modeling method was utilized to validate the hypotheses. Through an online survey, 100 valid samples were gathered from Indonesian live streaming users. The results showed that real time interaction and AR virtual try-on directly affect the immersive experience, and then drive impulse buying for viewers in live streaming e-commerce. Personalized product recommendations and immersive experiences directly influence impulse buying in live streaming e-commerce. These findings contribute to providing new insight of online retailers to create impulse buying when they do live streaming.

articleTitle: Estimation of Suitable Low-Frequency Passbands of MMFs using Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: In the investigation of multimode fibers (MMF) within the low-frequency spectrum, many passbands have been identified and can be estimated using approximation Mathematics. However, a significant challenge emerges in the precision of peak frequency estimation since this can lead to improper peak frequency selection in each passband for signal transmission, resulting in an unsuitable Bit Error Rate (BER) for optical communication systems. To overcome this problem, high-accuracy prediction is needed. Neural Networks (NN), a type of Artificial Intelligence (AI), can be used for estimation due to its performance in learning complex data. In this paper, the fitnet model is employed for estimating peak frequencies for passbands in the low-frequency region of MMF. The predicted peak frequencies are then applied to the orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) optical communication system, and the performance of the system is evaluated in terms of BER. Comparing the obtained BERs between the case of using NN and the case of using Mathematics approximation, it is found that the obtained BER from NN is lower than that from Mathematics approximation, especially for the data rate lower than 600 Mbps. This then shows the advantages of applying NN in finding the peak frequencies in low-frequency region of MMF.

articleTitle: Optimal Placement and Sizing of Photovoltaics to Supply Water Pumping Stations
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: This paper presents a stochastic optimization-based algorithm to perceive the location and size of multiple solar photovoltaic (PV) generations in a distribution network optimally, focusing on supplying water system loads. The presented algorithm accounts for the uncertainty of PV production and load power demand. The solar irradiance real data for three years is used to extract representative solar irradiance profiles on different days and seasons using the k-means clustering algorithm. An IEEE 33-bus radial distribution test network has been implemented for the case study, and water stations are located within this grid. The load demand of water transmission stations is predicted based on historical data, and the uncertainty is modeled employing the normal probability distribution function. The outcomes demonstrated that the proposed stochastic planning model effectively addresses the PV generation uncertainty and optimally identifies the placement and capacity of PV units.

articleTitle: System Development for Estimating Geolocation, Direction, and Velocity of Moving Objects in UAV Applications Using Monocular Camera
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) have become widely used across various fields, leading to an escalation in workload for UAV operators. Both computer vision and machine learning can significantly contribute to automating UAV operations. In UAV applications, e.g., traffic monitoring, object geolocation, direction, and velocity prove to be crucial data for effective UAV ground operations. This work introduces a system designed to detect and localize moving objects in UAV videos, using monocular camera. The proposed system is composed of four main parts: object detection, object tracking, object-depth estimation, and conversion of geolocation, direction, and velocity. Aiming for on-board implementation with limited resources, the selected algorithms prioritize processing speed over accuracy. For the first two main parts, the system utilizes YOLO and Lukas-Kanade algorithms respectively. It also employs k-nearest neighbors and polynomial regression along with MiDaS algorithm for object-depth inference models. The last part involves transforming position from the camera plane to the real world plane. Following testing of the proposed system at two UAV heights, it was found that the MiDaS with polynomial regression model performs better in geolocation and velocity estimation, al-though it exhibits slightly lower accuracy in estimating direction. This presents our initial step in developing the proposed system, with plans for system enhancement in the future.

articleTitle: Enhanced - Resolution Epileptogenic Zone Detection in 18F-FDG PET Imaging for Drug-Resistant Epilepsy Using a Siamese Network
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: Epilepsy, a complex neurological condition, is characterized by recurring seizures and often challenging diagnosis. This study aims to tackle this intricate problem by leveraging deep learning techniques. In the face of limited training data, we leverage the characteristics of a Siamese Convolutional Neural Network integrated with image enhancement and data augmentation strategies, aimed at enhancing the accuracy of epilepsy detection and localization. Our dataset consists of cases of epilepsy associated with hypometabolism. Notably, our results showcase the effectiveness of the Siamese Network, particularly when combined with the RAISR image enhancement technique and horizontal flip as a data augmentation method, yielding a promising recall score of 56%. Additionally, we conducted a detailed examination of the performance of these techniques within individual brain lobes, underlining the imperative need for region-specific approaches in epilepsy localization. This research not only contributes to the advancement of epilepsy detection but also underscores the significance of adapting methodologies to the unique attributes of various brain regions.

articleTitle: Developing a Treatment Method for Dementia and Delirium Patients using Virtual Reality
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: Virtual reality (VR) is a modern technology that has its applications in various domains of life and medical science is no exception. VR can be used to treat number of diseases such as Anxiety Disorders, Autism Spectrum Disorder, Postoperative Recovery, Mild cognitive Impairment (MCI) to name a few. The primary goal of this work is to develop a user-friendly therapy treatment software tool for Dementia and Delirium by employing VR. The developed tool can provide contemporary technology, and a meditation technique to improve concentration and cognitive function by providing a semi-immersive experience in a virtual environment. A mobile application, an APK version, has been created using React Native to provide a user-friendly, cost-effective experience for patients. Further, a remote monitoring system is built that provides an effortless way for medical professionals and caregivers to track their patients' improvement and progress. A specially trained neural network has been implemented to validate the data and receive comprehensible insights about the progress of patients who are treated with this treatment method for 2 months. This paper aims to describe the outcomes achieved by implementing this treatment method among dementia and dementia patients in Sri Lanka.

articleTitle: Wat Arun Metaverse: A Virtual Reality Based Approach for Digitization, Education, and Exploration of Cultural Heritage
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: Wat Arun, or the ‘Temple of Dawn,’ is a well-known Buddhist temple and a significant tourist destination in Thailand. The temple serves as a hub for research on Buddhist studies and rich Thai culture. Overcoming the limitations in traditional cultural preservation, and educational methods, this paper describes a transformative Virtual Reality (VR) based metaverse design to attract users to explore this historical landmark. The methodology involves advanced Three-Dimensional (3D) digitization techniques for 3D model optimization, and customization, and a gamified educational framework. Results show the preliminary stage of the overall process of 3D implementation on Wat Arun metaverse. This study contributes as a vital platform for educators, researchers, and enthusiasts seeking an authentic and interactive exploration of rich cultural heritages. By setting a precedent for immersive and engaging experiences in heritage exploration, this research extends the boundaries of how cultural sites can be understood, appreciated, and preserved in the digital era.

articleTitle: Wrist Angle Estimation Under Different Loads Condition Based on Multi-Layer Perceptron Neural Network and Surface Electromyography Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: This research focuses on the impact of load on wrist angle prediction using surface electromyographic (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$s$</tex> EMG) signals from forearm muscles, specifically considering the flexion-extension of the wrist The goal is to develop a model capable of accurately predicting wrist angles under various conditions. A multilayer perceptron neural network (MLPNN) has been constructed and tested, processing features extracted from the mean absolute value (MAV) of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$s$</tex> EMG signals. The experiments included a diverse simulation of load to examine the model's responsiveness to these forces. The findings indicate that the model can reliably predict wrist angles, evidenced by high R-squared values and low mean squared error (MSE) rates. This study suggests the potential for developing high-precision tools for human posture analysis and prediction that could be applied in a variety of situations, including research and potentially in physical therapy and prosthetic technologies in the future.

articleTitle: Spring Rolls' Size Inspection System Using Deep Image Processing
publicationTitle: 2024 21st International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
abstract: This conference paper presents a novel and efficient system for inspecting the size of spring rolls using advanced deep image processing techniques. With the increasing demand for high-quality food products in the food industry, ensuring the consistency and precision of dimensions in spring rolls is crucial for both manufacturers and consumers. Traditional inspection methods often fall short in accuracy and speed, motivating the exploration of innovative technologies such as deep learning. The proposed system leverages state-of-the-art deep neural networks to analyze high-resolution images of spring rolls captured during the manufacturing process. A convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture is employed to train on a diverse dataset of annotated spring roll images to accurately detect and measure the dimensions of individual rolls.
